NaN at x = 0, -1, -2.\nfn petir_psi(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    let y = abs(x);\n    if (x == 0.0 || x == -1.0 || x == -2.0) {\n        return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n    }\n    if (y >= 2.0) {\n        let c = petir_cheb_apsi_cs(8.0 / (y * y) - 1.0);\n        if (x < 0.0) {\n            let s = sin(PETIR_PSI_PI * x);\n            let co = cos(PETIR_PSI_PI * x);\n            if (abs(s) < 2.0 * PETIR_PSI_SQRT_MIN) {\n                return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n            }\n            return log(y) - 0.5 / x + c - PETIR_PSI_PI * co / s;\n        }\n        return log(y) - 0.5 / x + c;\n    }\n    if (x < -1.0) {\n        let v = x + 2.0;\n        return -(1.0 / x + 1.0 / (x + 1.0) + 1.0 / v) + petir_cheb_psi_cs(2.0 * v - 1.0);\n    }\n    if (x < 0.0) {\n        let v = x + 1.0;\n        return -(1.0 / x + 1.0 / v) + petir_cheb_psi_cs(2.0 * v - 1.0);\n    }\n    if (x < 1.0) {\n        return -1.0 / x + petir_cheb_psi_cs(2.0 * x - 1.0);\n    }\n    return petir_cheb_psi_cs(2.0 * (x - 1.0) - 1.0);\n}\n\n// Re psi(1 + i y). Ports `psi_1piy`. Even in y.\nfn petir_psi_1piy(y: f32) -> f32 {\n    let ay = abs(y);\n    if (ay > 1000.0) {\n        let yi2 = 1.0 / (ay * ay);\n        return log(ay) + yi2 * (1.0 / 12.0 + 1.0 / 120.0 * yi2 + 1.0 / 252.0 * yi2 * yi2);\n    }\n    if (ay > 10.0) {\n        let yi2 = 1.0 / (ay * ay);\n        let sum = yi2 * (1.0 / 12.0\n            + yi2 * (1.0 / 120.0\n            + yi2 * (1.0 / 252.0\n            + yi2 * (1.0 / 240.0\n            + yi2 * (1.0 / 132.0 + 691.0 / 32760.0 * yi2)))));\n        return log(ay) + sum;\n    }\n    if (ay > 1.0) {\n        let y2 = ay * ay;\n        let v = y2 * (1.0 / (1.0 + y2) + 0.5 / (4.0 + y2));\n        return petir_cheb_r1py((2.0 * ay - 11.0) / 9.0) - PETIR_PSI_EULER + v;\n    }\n    let y2 = y * y;\n    let p = 1.9603999466879846e-4\n        + y2 * (-3.8426659205114377e-8 + y2 * (1.0041592839497644e-11 - y2 * 2.951674376350019e-15));\n    var sum = 0.0;\n    for (var n: u32 = 1u; n <= 50u; n = n + 1u) {\n        let nf = f32(n);\n        sum = sum + 1.0 / (nf * (nf * nf + y2));\n    }\n    return -PETIR_PSI_EULER + y2 * (sum + p);\n}\n\n// The Hurwitz zeta zeta(s, q), s > 1 and q > 0. Ports `hzeta`.\n//\n// The f64 port\'s underflow and overflow guards are kept at their GSL values;\n// in f32 they simply never fire, and exp()/pow() produce 0 or inf of their\n// own accord at the corresponding f32 bounds.\nfn petir_hzeta(s: f32, q: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(s > 1.0) || !(q > 0.0)) {\n        return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n    }\n    let max_bits = 54.0;\n    if ((s > max_bits && q < 1.0) || (s > 0.5 * max_bits && q < 0.25)) {\n        return pow(q, -s);\n    }\n    if (s > 0.5 * max_bits && q < 1.0) {\n        return pow(q, -s) * (1.0 + pow(q / (1.0 + q), s) + pow(q / (2.0 + q), s));\n    }\n    let kmax = 10.0;\n    let pmax = pow(kmax + q, -s);\n    var scp = s;\n    var pcp = pmax / (kmax + q);\n    var ans = pmax * ((kmax + q) / (s - 1.0) + 0.5);\n    for (var k: u32 = 0u; k < 10u; k = k + 1u) {\n        ans = ans + pow(f32(k) + q, -s);\n    }\n    for (var j: u32 = 0u; j <= 12u; j = j + 1u) {\n        let delta = petir_hzeta_c(j + 1u) * scp * pcp;\n        ans = ans + delta;\n        if (abs(delta / ans) < 0.5 * 1.1920929e-7) {\n            break;\n        }\n        let jf = f32(j);\n        scp = scp * (s + 2.0 * jf + 1.0) * (s + 2.0 * jf + 2.0);\n        pcp = pcp / ((kmax + q) * (kmax + q));\n    }\n    return ans;\n}\n\n// zeta(s) for s >= 0, s != 1. Ports `riemann_zeta_sgt0`.\nfn petir_zeta_sgt0(s: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (s < 1.0) {\n        return petir_cheb_zeta_xlt1(2.0 * s - 1.0) / (s - 1.0);\n    }\n    if (s <= 20.0) {\n        return petir_cheb_zeta_xgt1((2.0 * s - 21.0) / 19.0) / (s - 1.0);\n    }\n    let f2 = 1.0 - pow(2.0, -s);\n    let f3 = 1.0 - pow(3.0, -s);\n    let f5 = 1.0 - pow(5.0, -s);\n    let f7 = 1.0 - pow(7.0, -s);\n    return 1.0 / (f2 * f3 * f5 * f7);\n}\n\n// zeta(1 - s) for s < 0. Ports `riemann_zeta_1ms_slt0`.\nfn petir_zeta_1ms_slt0(s: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (s > -19.0) {\n        return petir_cheb_zeta_xgt1((-19.0 - 2.0 * s) / 19.0) / (-s);\n    }\n    let f2 = 1.0 - pow(2.0, -(1.0 - s));\n    let f3 = 1.0 - pow(3.0, -(1.0 - s));\n    let f5 = 1.0 - pow(5.0, -(1.0 - s));\n    let f7 = 1.0 - pow(7.0, -(1.0 - s));\n    return 1.0 / (f2 * f3 * f5 * f7);\n}\n\n// The Riemann zeta function. Ports `zeta`. NaN at s = 1 and for s <= -34.\n//\n// REQUIRES gamma.wgsl for `petir_gamma`.\nfn petir_zeta(s: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (s == 1.0) {\n        return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n    }\n    if (s >= 0.0) {\n        return petir_zeta_sgt0(s);\n    }\n    let m = s % 2.0;\n    var sin_term = 0.0;\n    if (m != 0.0) {\n        sin_term = sin(0.5 * PETIR_PSI_PI * (s % 4.0)) / PETIR_PSI_PI;\n    }\n    if (sin_term == 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;  // the trivial zeros at the negative even integers\n    }\n    // f32 cannot carry the reflection branch below here -- see the header.\n    if (s <= -34.0) {\n        return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n    }\n    let n = u32(floor((-s) / 10.0));\n    let fs = s + 10.0 * f32(n);\n    let p = pow(2.0 * PETIR_PSI_PI, fs) / petir_twopi_pow(n);\n    return p * petir_gamma(1.0 - s) * sin_term * petir_zeta_1ms_slt0(s);\n}\n\n// zeta(s) - 1 without forming the difference. Ports `eta`. Finite at s = 1, where zeta is not.\nfn petir_eta(s: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (s > 100.0) {\n        return 1.0;\n    }\n    if (abs(s - 1.0) < 10.0 * PETIR_PSI_ROOT5_EPS) {\n        let del = s - 1.0;\n        let c1 = PETIR_PSI_LN2 * (PETIR_PSI_EULER - 0.5 * PETIR_PSI_LN2);\n        return PETIR_PSI_LN2 + del * (c1 + del * (-0.0326862962794493\n             + del * (0.001568991705415515 + del * 0.0007498724211204753)));\n    }\n    return (1.0 - exp((1.0 - s) * PETIR_PSI_LN2)) * petir_zeta(s);\n}\n\n// psi(1, x), the trigamma function. Ports `psi_1`.\n//\n// For x > 0 this is exactly zeta(2, x): GSL routes it through psi_n_xg0 with\n// n = 1, whose ln(1!) is zero, so the exp_mult collapses to the Hurwitz zeta.\nfn petir_psi_1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (x == 0.0 || x == -1.0 || x == -2.0) {\n        return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n    }\n    if (x > 0.0) {\n        return petir_hzeta(2.0, x);\n    }\n    if (x > -5.0) {\n        let m = -floor(x);\n        let fx = x + m;\n        if (fx == 0.0) {\n            return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n        }\n        var sum = 0.0;\n        let mi = u32(m);\n        for (var k: u32 = 0u; k < mi; k = k + 1u) {\n            let t = x + f32(k);\n            sum = sum + 1.0 / (t * t);\n        }\n        return petir_hzeta(2.0, fx) + sum;\n    }\n    let sp = sin(PETIR_PSI_PI * x);\n    return PETIR_PSI_PI * PETIR_PSI_PI / (sp * sp) - petir_hzeta(2.0, 1.0 - x);\n}\n";

#### Constant `DEBYE`

GSL's Debye functions `D_1` .. `D_6`, ported from `specfunc/debye.c` by
way of [`crate::specfunc::debye`].

Provides `petir_debye(n, x)` and the six Chebyshev series behind it.
`D_3` is the Debye heat-capacity function.

**Two machine constants are retargeted to `f32`** — GSL's `xcut` and the
sum/closed-form cut are derived from `f64`'s range and mean nothing here.
See [`mirror_debye`]; the retargeting shortens the inner loop eight-fold
at no measured cost.

}\n    return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n}\n\n// The f32 small-argument cut. D_1 uses 2 sqrt(eps); the rest 2 sqrt(2)\n// sqrt(eps) -- upstream\'s own asymmetry, retargeted to f32\'s epsilon.\nfn petir_debye_small_cut(n: u32) -> f32 {\n    let se = 3.4526698e-4;  // sqrt(f32::EPSILON)\n    if (n == 1u) { return 2.0 * se; }\n    return 2.0 * 1.4142135623730951 * se;\n}\n\nfn petir_debye_pow_n(x: f32, n: u32) -> f32 {\n    var out = 1.0;\n    for (var k: u32 = 0u; k < n; k = k + 1u) { out = out * x; }\n    return out;\n}\n\n// D_n(x) for n in 1 ..= 6. NaN for x < 0 or an untabulated order.\nfn petir_debye(n: u32, x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (n == 0u || n > 6u) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (!(x >= 0.0)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    let lin = petir_debye_lin(n);\n    if (x < petir_debye_small_cut(n)) {\n        return 1.0 - lin * x + petir_debye_quad(n) * x * x;\n    }\n    if (x <= 4.0) {\n        return petir_debye_cheb(n, x * x / 8.0 - 1.0) - lin * x;\n    }\n    let vinf = petir_debye_vinf(n);\n    if (x < PETIR_DEBYE_SUMCUT) {\n        let nexp = floor(PETIR_DEBYE_XCUT / x);\n        let ex = exp(-x);\n        var sum = 0.0;\n        var rk = nexp;\n        var i = nexp;\n        loop {\n            if (i < 1.0) { break; }\n            // xk = rk * x, RECOMPUTED rather than decremented -- see the\n            // header. Upstream carries `xk -= x` down the loop, which is\n            // exact enough in f64 and drifts badly in f32.\n            let xk = rk * x;\n            sum = sum * ex;\n            sum = sum + petir_debye_fall(n, 1.0 / xk) / rk;\n            rk = rk - 1.0;\n            i = i - 1.0;\n        }\n        return vinf / petir_debye_pow_n(x, n) - f32(n) * sum * ex;\n    }\n    if (x < PETIR_DEBYE_XCUT) {\n        return (vinf - f32(n) * petir_debye_fall_x(n, x) * exp(-x))\n             / petir_debye_pow_n(x, n);\n    }\n    return vinf / petir_debye_pow_n(x, n);\n}\n";

#### Constant `DILOG`

GSL's real dilogarithm `Li_2(x)`, ported from `specfunc/dilog.c` by way of
[`crate::specfunc::dilog`].

Provides `petir_dilog(x)` for all real `x`, returning the **real part** of
the principal branch above the branch point at `x = 1`.

**No coefficient tables** — two convergent series and seven branch
identities — so unlike the other specfunc shaders this one has no
generator and no table audit. See [`mirror_dilog`].

```rust
pub const DILOG: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::dilog`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/dilog.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000, 2004 Gerard Jungman.\n//\n// Li_2(x) = sum_{k>=1} x^k / k^2  =  -integral_0^x ln(1-t)/t dt, for real x.\n// GSL\'s convention: Li_2(1) = pi^2/6, Li_2(0) = 0. Conventions differ; check\n// before comparing against a table.\n//\n// NO COEFFICIENT TABLES. Unlike bessel/psi_zeta/debye this kernel has none --\n// it is two convergent series and seven branch identities. So there is no\n// generator and no table audit for it, and `mirror_dilog` is written by hand\n// beside this file rather than emitted from one parse. The three constants\n// that do appear (pi^2/6, pi^2/3, and the 0.01 cut) are checked against each\n// other by `every_generated_shader_and_its_mirror_hold_the_same_constants`\'s\n// sibling test rather than by the table audit.\n//\n// A PREDICTION THAT WAS REFUTED, AND UPSTREAM\'S CONSTANT KEPT BECAUSE OF IT.\n//\n// petir_dilog_series_2 switches at x = 0.01 between evaluating\n// (1-x)ln(1-x)/x directly and using its Taylor expansion through x^8. The\n// expectation, by analogy with debye.wgsl where two f64 thresholds HAD to be\n// retargeted, was that 0.01 would be far too small in f32: the branch then\n// forms 1 + t with t near -1, an 8th-order cancellation, and f32 has seven\n// digits to lose rather than sixteen. The Taylor truncation error is ~x^9/10,\n// which reaches f32 epsilon only near x = 0.22, so there looked to be two\n// decades of headroom.\n//\n// MEASURED, and it is not so. Worst relative error against the f64 module\n// over x in [-15, 15] where |Li_2| > 0.1, as a function of the cut:\n//\n//   0.01 (upstream, shipped)   4.786e-06\n//   0.05                       4.786e-06\n//   0.1                        4.063e-06\n//   0.2                        4.063e-06\n//   0.3                        2.472e-05\n//   0.5                        2.472e-05\n//\n// The best available gain is 1.18x, and past 0.25 the Taylor branch is being\n// asked for arguments it was never meant to cover and the error grows\n// five-fold. So UPSTREAM\'S 0.01 IS KEPT: a 1.18x gain does not justify\n// departing from a literal transcription, and the two decades of headroom the\n// prediction was built on do not exist.\n//\n// The general rule this and debye.wgsl together make is \"know which of\n// upstream\'s constants still mean something in f32\", not \"always retarget\"\n// and not \"always keep\". debye.wgsl\'s xcut is derived from f64\'s EXPONENT\n// RANGE, which f32 does not share, so it had to move. This cut is derived\n// from a TRUNCATION ORDER against epsilon, and moving it buys nothing because\n// the error is dominated elsewhere.\n//\n// WHERE THE f32 ERROR ACTUALLY IS: the x > 2 branch, and Li_2\'s zero.\n//\n// Per branch, worst relative against the f64 module where |Li_2| > 0.1:\n//\n//   x in (0, 0.25]     3.021e-07      direct power series\n//   x in (0.25, 0.5]   6.982e-07      accelerated series\n//   x in (0.5, 1)      3.553e-07      Landen reflection\n//   x in (1, 1.01]     4.244e-08      the eps/ln(eps) expansion\n//   x in (1.01, 2]     1.561e-07      1 - 1/x Landen\n//   x in (2, 40]       5.710e-06      inversion            <- the outlier\n//   x in [-40, 0)      4.510e-07      duplication\n//\n// Six of the seven are one f32 ulp. The inversion branch is twenty times\n// worse and it is CANCELLATION, not transcription: it forms\n// pi^2/3 - Li_2(1/x) - (1/2)ln^2 x, and 0.5*ln^2(x) passes through pi^2/3 at\n// x = 12.5952 -- where Li_2 has its real zero. Every implementation in every\n// precision loses relative accuracy there; f64 simply has more digits to\n// spend. The bounded quantity is the ABSOLUTE error, measured at 1.871e-06\n// over x in [-15, 15].\n//\n// A CALLER WANTING Li_2 NEAR x = 12.6 IN f32 SHOULD EXPECT NO CORRECT DIGITS,\n// and that is a property of the formula, not of this port.\n\nconst PETIR_DILOG_ZETA2: f32 = 1.6449341;      // pi^2 / 6\nconst PETIR_DILOG_PI2_3: f32 = 3.2898681;      // pi^2 / 3\nconst PETIR_DILOG_EPS:   f32 = 1.1920929e-7;   // f32::EPSILON\n// The logarithmic/Taylor cut inside petir_dilog_series_2. UPSTREAM\'S VALUE,\n// kept deliberately -- see the header.\nconst PETIR_DILOG_TCUT:  f32 = 0.01;\n\n// sum_{k>=1} x^k / k^2, converging usefully only for |x| < 1/2. Upstream\'s\n// dilog_series_1. The term is carried by the ratio ((k-1)/k)^2 rather than\n// recomputed, which is upstream\'s own structure.\nfn petir_dilog_series_1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var sum = x;\n    var term = x;\n    for (var k: i32 = 2; k < 1000; k = k + 1) {\n        let rk = (f32(k) - 1.0) / f32(k);\n        term = term * x;\n        term = term * rk * rk;\n        sum = sum + term;\n        if (abs(term / sum) < PETIR_DILOG_EPS) { break; }\n    }\n    return sum;\n}\n\n// sum_{k>=1} r^k / (k^2 (k+1)), upstream\'s series_2. The first eight terms are\n// unconditional before the convergence test begins, which is upstream\'s own\n// two-loop structure: a ratio test against a part-summed series is meaningless\n// while the sum is still small.\nfn petir_dilog_series_2_raw(r: f32) -> f32 {\n    var rk = r;\n    var sum = 0.5 * r;\n    for (var k: i32 = 2; k < 10; k = k + 1) {\n        rk = rk * r;\n        sum = sum + rk / (f32(k) * f32(k) * (f32(k) + 1.0));\n    }\n    for (var k: i32 = 10; k < 100; k = k + 1) {\n        rk = rk * r;\n        let ds = rk / (f32(k) * f32(k) * (f32(k) + 1.0));\n        sum = sum + ds;\n        if (abs(ds / sum) < 0.5 * PETIR_DILOG_EPS) { break; }\n    }\n    return sum;\n}\n\n// Li_2(x) = 1 + (1-x) ln(1-x) / x + series_2(x), for -1 < x < 1.\n// Every call site below supplies x in [0, 1/2].\nfn petir_dilog_series_2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    let s = petir_dilog_series_2_raw(x);\n    var t: f32;\n    if (x > PETIR_DILOG_TCUT) {\n        t = (1.0 - x) * log(1.0 - x) / x;\n    } else {\n        // Taylor of (1-x)ln(1-x)/x about 0, through x^8.\n        let t68 = 1.0 / 6.0 + x * (1.0 / 7.0 + x * (1.0 / 8.0));\n        let t38 = 1.0 / 3.0 + x * (1.0 / 4.0 + x * (1.0 / 5.0 + x * t68));\n        t = (x - 1.0) * (1.0 + x * (0.5 + x * t38));\n    }\n    return s + 1.0 + t;\n}\n\n// Li_2(x) for x >= 0. Seven branches, upstream\'s dilog_xge0.\nfn petir_dilog_xge0(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (x > 2.0) {\n        let log_x = log(x);\n        return PETIR_DILOG_PI2_3 - petir_dilog_series_2(1.0 / x) - 0.5 * log_x * log_x;\n    }\n    if (x > 1.01) {\n        let log_x = log(x);\n        let log_term = log_x * (log(1.0 - 1.0 / x) + 0.5 * log_x);\n        return PETIR_DILOG_ZETA2 + petir_dilog_series_2(1.0 - 1.0 / x) - log_term;\n    }\n    if (x > 1.0) {\n        // Series about x = 1, in eps AND ln(eps): Li_2 is not analytic there,\n        // so a plain Taylor series cannot work.\n        let eps = x - 1.0;\n        let lne = log(eps);\n        let c1 = 1.0 - lne;\n        let c2 = -(1.0 - 2.0 * lne) / 4.0;\n        let c3 = (1.0 - 3.0 * lne) / 9.0;\n        let c4 = -(1.0 - 4.0 * lne) / 16.0;\n        let c5 = (1.0 - 5.0 * lne) / 25.0;\n        let c6 = -(1.0 - 6.0 * lne) / 36.0;\n        let c7 = (1.0 - 7.0 * lne) / 49.0;\n        let c8 = -(1.0 - 8.0 * lne) / 64.0;\n        return PETIR_DILOG_ZETA2 + eps * (c1 + eps * (c2 + eps * (c3 + eps * (c4\n             + eps * (c5 + eps * (c6 + eps * (c7 + eps * c8)))))));\n    }\n    if (x == 1.0) { return PETIR_DILOG_ZETA2; }\n    if (x > 0.5) {\n        let log_x = log(x);\n        return PETIR_DILOG_ZETA2 - petir_dilog_series_2(1.0 - x) - log_x * log(1.0 - x);\n    }\n    if (x > 0.25) { return petir_dilog_series_2(x); }\n    if (x > 0.0)  { return petir_dilog_series_1(x); }\n    return 0.0;\n}\n\n// Li_2(x) for real x. Negative arguments go through upstream\'s duplication\n// formula, Li_2(-y) = (1/2) Li_2(y^2) - Li_2(y), so both inner calls take a\n// non-negative argument and the recursion is one level deep.\n//\n// Returns the REAL PART of the principal branch for x > 1; Li_2 is complex\n// there and neither GSL nor this reports the imaginary part. NaN propagates.\nfn petir_dilog(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x >= 0.0) { return petir_dilog_xge0(x); }\n    return -petir_dilog_xge0(-x) + 0.5 * petir_dilog_xge0(x * x);\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `AIRY`

GSL's Airy functions `Ai`, `Bi` and their exponentially scaled forms,
ported from `specfunc/airy.c` by way of [`crate::specfunc::airy`].

Thirteen Chebyshev series, 281 coefficients. **Prefer the scaled entry
points on a GPU:** `petir_airy_bi` overflows `f32` near `x = 25.9` where
the `f64` module reaches 104.1, and `petir_airy_bi_scaled` does not
overflow at all.

```rust
pub const AIRY: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::airy`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/airy.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman. The underlying Chebyshev\n//   expansions are SLATEC\'s (ai, aie, bi, bie), which GSL vendored.\n//\n// Ai(x) and Bi(x) solve y\'\' - x y = 0: Ai decays as x -> +inf, Bi grows, and\n// both oscillate as x -> -inf with slowly increasing wavelength. They are the\n// canonical turning-point functions.\n//\n// EVERY COEFFICIENT WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the f64 module -- 281\n// literals across thirteen Chebyshev series -- and the same script emits\n// `wgsl::mirror_airy`, so the shader and its CPU mirror cannot disagree about\n// a constant. The f64 module\'s own tables are audited bit-for-bit against\n// GSL\'s source by tests/gsl_tables_audit.rs.\n//\n// THE ORDER MATTERS AND WAS NOT GUESSED. In airy.c the data arrays are not\n// named after the series that use them -- aif_cs points at ai_data_f, bif_cs\n// at data_bif, aip_cs at data_aip. The extraction read the cheb_series\n// declarations; guessing would have mis-paired four of the thirteen.\n//\n// WHAT f32 COSTS HERE, AND WHERE. Measured against the f64 module; the full\n// per-branch table is in mirror_airy. The short version is that the\n// oscillatory branch below x = -1 is the expensive one, and it is the PHASE,\n// not the modulus, that costs: theta grows like (2/3)|x|^{3/2}, so by\n// x = -30 it is about 110 radians, where one f32 ulp is already 7.6e-06 rad.\n// cos and sin then carry that straight into the answer, and WGSL specifies\n// its trigonometric builtins to an ABSOLUTE 2^-11 inside [-pi, pi] with the\n// behaviour outside left to the implementation -- so a conforming device may\n// be much further out than llvmpipe is here.\n//\n// PREFER THE SCALED ENTRY POINTS ON A GPU. petir_airy_bi overflows f32 near\n// x = 26.07 where the f64 module reaches x = 104.1; petir_airy_bi_scaled does\n// not overflow at all, and petir_airy_ai_scaled stays representable far past\n// where petir_airy_ai has underflowed to zero. This is the same advice\n// bessel.wgsl gives for I_0_scaled, for the same reason.\n//\n// THE OVERFLOW GUARD CARRIES GSL\'S f64 CONSTANT AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.\n// Retargeting it to the f32 analogue of the same inequality (x = 25.87) was\n// predicted to be necessary, by analogy with debye.wgsl. It is not merely\n// unnecessary -- it is WRONG: over x in (25.87, 26.07) it would return +inf\n// for values between 3.6e37 and 7.8e37, all representable in an f32 whose\n// maximum is 3.4e38. Upstream\'s constant never fires before exp() genuinely\n// overflows. Measured table in mirror_airy.\n//\n// NOTE ON BIT-IDENTITY: these series are held in inline array<f32, N>\n// literals, which docs/wgsl-coverage.md records as costing GPU/CPU\n// bit-identity even in a branch that calls no transcendental. Do not expect\n// exact agreement with the mirror; the budgets in tests/wgsl_gpu.rs are set\n// accordingly.\n\nconst PETIR_AIRY_PI_4: f32 = 0.7853982;    // pi/4\n\n// GSL\'s am21 series, 37 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_am21(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 21>(\n        0.006580919027328491, 0.002367598470300436, 0.0001324741606367752,\n        1.5760089809191413e-05, 2.752970203800942e-06, 6.102678753450164e-07,\n        1.5950884346693783e-07, 4.710339496227789e-08, 1.529338788941459e-08,\n        5.359072297039802e-09, 2.0000909817241563e-09, 7.872292262511849e-10,\n        3.243103008365722e-10, 1.390105947018938e-10, 6.170110256054073e-11,\n        2.8249099240373887e-11, 1.329790010745624e-11, 6.418799953361587e-12,\n        3.1696999625713262e-12, 1.5981000160356085e-12, 8.213000050015518e-13,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 20; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s ath1 series, 36 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_ath1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 16>(\n        -0.07125838100910187, -0.005904719699174166, -0.0001211454436997883,\n        -9.886085535981692e-06, -1.3808410130877746e-06, -2.6142640763282543e-07,\n        -6.05043268819827e-08, -1.618436229477993e-08, -4.834649125484702e-09,\n        -1.5765526661937201e-09, -5.523151935804549e-10, -2.0545440349017952e-10,\n        -8.043411769964592e-11, -3.291251993164934e-11, -1.399875007579432e-11,\n        -6.161510104213397e-12,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 15; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s am22 series, 33 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_am22(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 16>(\n        -0.015628444030880928, 0.007783364504575729, 0.0008670577662996948,\n        0.00015696627087891102, 3.563962673069909e-05, 9.245983164873905e-06,\n        2.621101657496183e-06, 7.918822007013659e-07, 2.5104154133259726e-07,\n        8.265223527814669e-08, 2.8057115741830785e-08, 9.768211128857729e-09,\n        3.47407924650156e-09, 1.2582813679884453e-09, 4.629882588425005e-10,\n        1.7272824837100131e-10,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 15; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s ath2 series, 32 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_ath2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 17>(\n        0.004405273590236902, -0.030429193750023842, -0.001385653275065124,\n        -0.000180444389116019, -3.380847192602232e-05, -7.678183465031907e-06,\n        -1.967839352801093e-06, -5.483727250066295e-07, -1.625461578669274e-07,\n        -5.053049889625072e-08, -1.631580737182503e-08, -5.434204197740655e-09,\n        -1.857398568283486e-09, -6.489512260898778e-10, -2.310594771071095e-10,\n        -8.363282288925689e-11, -3.071196075232763e-11,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 16; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s aif series, 9 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_aif(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 9>(\n        -0.03797135874629021, 0.05919189006090164, 0.0009862928418442607,\n        6.8488438955682795e-06, 2.59420254167253e-08, 6.176612693531425e-11,\n        1.0092453809522686e-13, 1.2014000333477736e-16, 9.999999682655225e-20,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 8; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s aig series, 8 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_aig(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 8>(\n        0.01815236546099186, 0.02157256379723549, 0.0002567835617810488, 1.4265214076658594e-06,\n        4.5721151309408015e-09, 9.525169715474124e-12, 1.3919999694740875e-14,\n        9.99999983775159e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 7; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s bif series, 9 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_bif(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 9>(\n        -0.01673021726310253, 0.10252335667610168, 0.0017083092825487256,\n        1.1862545761687215e-05, 4.493290717277887e-08, 1.0698206903692054e-10,\n        1.748064312658698e-13, 2.0809999415861237e-16, 1.7999999428779406e-19,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 8; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s big series, 8 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_big(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 8>(\n        0.022466223686933517, 0.03736477717757225, 0.00044476217590272427,\n        2.4708076580282068e-06, 7.91913556952295e-09, 1.6498070271042664e-11,\n        2.411000002075503e-14, 1.999999967550318e-17,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 7; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s bif2 series, 10 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_bif2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 10>(\n        0.09984572976827621, 0.47862496972084045, 0.025155212730169296, 0.0005820693913847208,\n        7.499766070395708e-06, 6.134602870133676e-08, 3.4627539724496614e-10,\n        1.4288909682205753e-12, 4.496199961824543e-15, 1.1100000332756245e-17,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 9; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s big2 series, 10 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_big2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 10>(\n        0.033305663615465164, 0.16130921244621277, 0.006319007370620966, 0.0001187904563266784,\n        1.3045346349827014e-06, 9.374126364036783e-09, 4.745802015260203e-11,\n        1.7831069466008737e-13, 5.166999975226942e-16, 1.0999999780167719e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 9; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s aip series, 36 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_aip(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 36>(\n        -0.018751930445432663, -0.009144384413957596, 0.0009010457433760166,\n        -0.000139418407343328, 2.738158218562603e-05, -6.2750423239776865e-06,\n        1.6064843748608837e-06, -4.4763922346646723e-07, 1.3346358684884763e-07,\n        -4.2073533990105716e-08, 1.3902199391679915e-08, -4.783184959222808e-09,\n        1.704789753809166e-09, -6.268389696195698e-10, 2.3698243367675786e-10,\n        -9.186411353834245e-11, 3.6427853788989495e-11, -1.474755560726404e-11,\n        6.0851007392670464e-12, -2.5552771704129285e-12, 1.0906186977827081e-12,\n        -4.725870302729751e-13, 2.0769691034313448e-13, -9.249762414342833e-14,\n        4.1709670927595616e-14, -1.9029909755201996e-14, 8.779067899619512e-15,\n        -4.092755627948478e-15, 1.927106892913124e-15, -9.16019863280782e-16,\n        4.3935670442485483e-16, -2.1255030526348646e-16, 1.0367349755169655e-16,\n        -5.096419896105794e-17, 2.523770069674405e-17, -1.2579300361744028e-17,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 35; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s bip series, 24 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_bip(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 24>(\n        -0.083220474421978, 0.011461189016699791, 0.000428964413003996, -0.00014906639989931136,\n        -1.3076597497274633e-05, 6.327598384814337e-06, -4.2226696450597956e-07,\n        -1.9147186947066075e-07, 6.453106493609084e-08, -7.84485454374817e-09,\n        -9.607721285220805e-10, 7.000471313745038e-10, -1.773178964770139e-10,\n        2.2720889406024902e-11, 1.6540399692260843e-12, -1.8517099745901655e-12,\n        5.957599864825358e-13, -1.2194000149901019e-13, 1.3339999813339123e-14,\n        1.7200000316502776e-15, -1.4500000211417337e-15, 4.899999837780218e-16,\n        -1.0999999986962872e-16, 9.99999983775159e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 23; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s bip2 series, 29 coefficients.\nfn petir_airy_cheb_bip2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 29>(\n        -0.11359673738479614, 0.004138147458434105, 0.0001353470579488203,\n        1.0427316738059744e-05, 1.3474955267156474e-06, 1.696537452744451e-07,\n        -1.0096500524525709e-08, -1.6729119423075645e-08, -4.5815364835277705e-09,\n        3.7366812422057194e-10, 5.766930266659642e-10, 6.218126707979721e-11,\n        -6.329411994521195e-11, -1.491504836304003e-11, 7.88962124798065e-12,\n        2.4960513256983008e-12, -1.21300745056091e-12, -3.740492887215757e-13,\n        2.237727012152288e-13, 4.749019984228754e-14, -4.5261598559821065e-14,\n        -3.0171999677885454e-15, 9.105799847594544e-15, -9.814000071387365e-16,\n        -1.6429000222967574e-15, 5.532999735361973e-16, 2.1749999523032617e-16,\n        -1.737000009371451e-16, -1.000000045813705e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 28; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// Airy modulus and phase for x <= -1. Returns vec2(modulus, phase).\n//\n// Below -1 both functions oscillate, and a Chebyshev series in x directly\n// would need more terms as the oscillation tightens. M and theta are smooth\n// in 16/x^3, which is why this decomposition exists at all.\nfn petir_airy_mod_phase(x: f32) -> vec2<f32> {\n    var m: f32;\n    var p: f32;\n    if (x < -2.0) {\n        let z = 16.0 / (x * x * x) + 1.0;\n        m = petir_airy_cheb_am21(z);\n        p = petir_airy_cheb_ath1(z);\n    } else if (x <= -1.0) {\n        let z = (16.0 / (x * x * x) + 9.0) / 7.0;\n        m = petir_airy_cheb_am22(z);\n        p = petir_airy_cheb_ath2(z);\n    } else {\n        return vec2<f32>(bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u), bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u));\n    }\n    let mm = 0.3125 + m;\n    let pp = -0.625 + p;\n    let sqx = sqrt(-x);\n    return vec2<f32>(sqrt(mm / sqx), PETIR_AIRY_PI_4 - x * sqx * pp);\n}\n\n// exp(+(2/3) x^{3/2}) Ai(x), for x >= 1. Upstream\'s airy_aie.\nfn petir_airy_aie(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    let sqx = sqrt(x);\n    let z = 2.0 / (x * sqx) - 1.0;\n    let y = sqrt(sqx);\n    return (0.28125 + petir_airy_cheb_aip(z)) / y;\n}\n\n// exp(-(2/3) x^{3/2}) Bi(x), for x >= 2. Upstream\'s airy_bie, two\n// sub-branches at x = 4. ATR and BTR are upstream\'s own constants.\nfn petir_airy_bie(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    let sqx = sqrt(x);\n    let y = sqrt(sqx);\n    var c: f32;\n    if (x < 4.0) {\n        c = petir_airy_cheb_bip(8.750691 / (x * sqx) - 2.0938363);\n    } else {\n        c = petir_airy_cheb_bip2(16.0 / (x * sqx) - 1.0);\n    }\n    return (0.625 + c) / y;\n}\n\n// Ai(x) for all real x. NaN propagates; underflows to zero on the positive\n// axis and never overflows.\nfn petir_airy_ai(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x < -1.0) {\n        let mp = petir_airy_mod_phase(x);\n        return mp.x * cos(mp.y);\n    }\n    if (x <= 1.0) {\n        let z = x * x * x;\n        return 0.375 + (petir_airy_cheb_aif(z) - x * (0.25 + petir_airy_cheb_aig(z)));\n    }\n    let x32 = x * sqrt(x);\n    return petir_airy_aie(x) * exp(-2.0 * x32 / 3.0);\n}\n\n// exp(+(2/3) x^{3/2}) Ai(x) for x > 0, and plain Ai(x) for x <= 0 where the\n// function oscillates and needs no scaling. That asymmetry is upstream\'s.\nfn petir_airy_ai_scaled(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x < -1.0) {\n        let mp = petir_airy_mod_phase(x);\n        return mp.x * cos(mp.y);\n    }\n    if (x <= 1.0) {\n        let z = x * x * x;\n        let v = 0.375 + (petir_airy_cheb_aif(z) - x * (0.25 + petir_airy_cheb_aig(z)));\n        if (x > 0.0) { return v * exp(2.0 / 3.0 * sqrt(z)); }\n        return v;\n    }\n    return petir_airy_aie(x);\n}\n\n// Bi(x) for all real x. OVERFLOWS TO +inf on the positive axis -- near\n// x = 25.9 in f32, against x = 104.1 in f64. Use petir_airy_bi_scaled there.\n//\n// The guard below carries GSL\'s f64 threshold unchanged. In f32 it never\n// fires before exp() has overflowed on its own, so it is redundant rather\n// than wrong -- see mirror_airy, which measures that and keeps it as the more\n// literal transcription.\nfn petir_airy_bi(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x < -1.0) {\n        let mp = petir_airy_mod_phase(x);\n        return mp.x * sin(mp.y);\n    }\n    if (x < 1.0) {\n        let z = x * x * x;\n        return 0.625 + petir_airy_cheb_bif(z) + x * (0.4375 + petir_airy_cheb_big(z));\n    }\n    if (x <= 2.0) {\n        let z = (2.0 * x * x * x - 9.0) / 7.0;\n        return 1.125 + petir_airy_cheb_bif2(z) + x * (0.625 + petir_airy_cheb_big2(z));\n    }\n    let y = 2.0 * x * sqrt(x) / 3.0;\n    // GSL_LOG_DBL_MAX - 1, upstream\'s own bound, kept deliberately.\n    if (y > 708.3964) {\n        return bitcast<f32>(0x7f800000u);\n    }\n    return petir_airy_bie(x) * exp(y);\n}\n\n// exp(-(2/3) x^{3/2}) Bi(x) for x > 0, plain Bi(x) for x <= 0. Note the\n// exponent\'s sign is the OPPOSITE of ai_scaled\'s, because Bi grows where Ai\n// decays. Never overflows.\nfn petir_airy_bi_scaled(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x < -1.0) {\n        let mp = petir_airy_mod_phase(x);\n        return mp.x * sin(mp.y);\n    }\n    if (x < 1.0) {\n        let z = x * x * x;\n        let v = 0.625 + petir_airy_cheb_bif(z) + x * (0.4375 + petir_airy_cheb_big(z));\n        if (x > 0.0) { return v * exp(-2.0 / 3.0 * sqrt(z)); }\n        return v;\n    }\n    if (x <= 2.0) {\n        let x3 = x * x * x;\n        let z = (2.0 * x3 - 9.0) / 7.0;\n        let s = exp(-2.0 / 3.0 * sqrt(x3));\n        return s * (1.125 + petir_airy_cheb_bif2(z) + x * (0.625 + petir_airy_cheb_big2(z)));\n    }\n    return petir_airy_bie(x);\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `LAMBERT`

GSL's Lambert `W`, both real branches, ported from `specfunc/lambert.c`
by way of [`crate::specfunc::lambert`].

**One constant is retargeted to `f32` and it is load-bearing:** the
iteration's convergence tolerance. Upstream's `DBL_EPSILON` can never be
met by an `f32` iterate, so the loop would never stop early. See
[`mirror_lambert`].

```rust
pub const LAMBERT: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::lambert`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/lambert.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 2007 Brian Gough; from code donated by K. Briggs.\n//   Lambert-ology from Corless, Gonnet, Hare and Jeffrey, \"On Lambert\'s W\n//   Function\"; the Halley step is that paper\'s equation 5.12.\n//\n// W(x) solves W e^W = x. Two real branches: W_0 on [-1/e, inf) with values\n// >= -1, and W_{-1} on [-1/e, 0) with values <= -1. They meet at x = -1/e,\n// where W = -1 and dW/dx is infinite.\n//\n// THE ITERATION IS NOT PURELY HALLEY, AND THAT IS UPSTREAM\'S CHOICE. For\n// w > 0 it takes a plain Newton step; only for w <= 0 does it take the Halley\n// step with its second-order correction. On the positive branch p = w+1 is\n// bounded away from zero and Newton converges on its own; near w = -1 the\n// Halley denominator is what keeps the step finite.\n//\n// UPSTREAM\'S STOPPING RULE IS WRONG TWICE OVER AT f32 WIDTH, in two\n// different ways. The rule is  |t| < 10 * eps * max(|w|, 1/(|p| e^w)).\n//\n// 1. eps IS A PRECISION CONSTANT AND IS RETARGETED to f32::EPSILON\n//    (1.19e-07). With DBL_EPSILON (2.2e-16) an f32 iterate can never satisfy\n//    the test at all: measured over 200 W_0 probes, 142 burn the full\n//    iteration budget and the other 58 stop only because their step became\n//    EXACTLY ZERO -- all 58, checked -- which satisfies any positive\n//    tolerance. The rule never terminates the loop; the loop runs out, or\n//    the arithmetic does.\n//\n// 2. THE 1/(|p| e^w) TERM IS DROPPED, because it makes the tolerance O(1).\n//    Once w is very negative e^w is tiny and the term explodes: at\n//    x = -2.1e-06, w is about -15.8 and the tolerance comes out at 5.947e-01\n//    against 1.885e-05 without it -- over a hundred times the 0.005 step it\n//    then accepts, stopping a full iteration early with w wrong in the third\n//    decimal. In f64 the same expression gives 2.9e-10 and is harmless,\n//    which is why upstream carries it.\n//\n//    Measured over the whole W_{-1} domain down to x = -1e-07:\n//      upstream\'s rule, eps retargeted:  4.769e-03 worst, 7 iterations\n//      10 * eps * |w|          SHIPPED:  9.982e-07 worst, 8 iterations\n//    One extra iteration for three and a half orders, with W_0 untouched at\n//    3.071e-07 either way. Safe near the branch point because the iteration\n//    is not entered there -- the sqrt(q) series handles it.\n//\n// THESE ARE TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF DECISION, and airy.wgsl makes a third.\n// Point 1 retargets a PRECISION CONSTANT whose f64 value is unreachable.\n// Point 2 changes a FORMULA that is numerically inadequate at f32 width, as\n// debye.wgsl does for its xk counter. airy.wgsl KEEPS GSL\'s f64 overflow\n// threshold, because that is a RANGE GUARD and retargeting it would discard\n// representable answers. Know what the constant is FOR.\n//\n// THE ITERATION COUNTS ARE UPSTREAM\'S (10 for W_0, 32 for W_{-1}) and are\n// kept. In f32 convergence is reached far sooner, so they are ceilings that\n// are not approached rather than tuning.\n//\n// NO COEFFICIENT TABLES except the 12-term series near the branch point,\n// which is held inline; see the note in airy.wgsl about what that costs in\n// GPU/CPU bit-identity.\n\nconst PETIR_LAMBERT_ONE_OVER_E: f32 = 0.36787945;\nconst PETIR_LAMBERT_E: f32 = 2.7182817;\n// f32::EPSILON -- RETARGETED from upstream\'s DBL_EPSILON, see the header.\nconst PETIR_LAMBERT_EPS: f32 = 1.1920929e-7;\n\n// The series in r = sqrt(q) near the branch point, q = x + 1/e. Both branches\n// share it and differ only in the sign of r: W_0 takes +sqrt(q), W_{-1} takes\n// -sqrt(q), which is the two sides of the square-root branch point.\n// Upstream\'s nested grouping is reproduced; a different association would\n// give a different last bit.\nfn petir_lambert_series(r: f32) -> f32 {\n    let c0  = -1.0;\n    let c1  = 2.331644;\n    let c2  = -1.8121879;\n    let c3  = 1.9366311;\n    let c4  = -2.3535512;\n    let c5  = 3.066859;\n    let c6  = -4.1753354;\n    let c7  = 5.8580236;\n    let c8  = -8.401032;\n    let c9  = 12.250754;\n    let c10 = -18.100697;\n    let c11 = 27.029045;\n    let t8 = c8 + r * (c9 + r * (c10 + r * c11));\n    let t5 = c5 + r * (c6 + r * (c7 + r * t8));\n    let t1 = c1 + r * (c2 + r * (c3 + r * (c4 + r * t5)));\n    return c0 + r * t1;\n}\n\n// Upstream\'s halley_iteration. Returns NaN if it does not converge, which\n// upstream reports as GSL_EMAXITER and comments \"should never get here\".\nfn petir_lambert_halley(x: f32, w_initial: f32, max_iters: i32) -> f32 {\n    var w = w_initial;\n    for (var i: i32 = 0; i < max_iters; i = i + 1) {\n        let e = exp(w);\n        let p = w + 1.0;\n        var t = w * e - x;\n        if (w > 0.0) {\n            t = (t / p) / e;                       // Newton\n        } else {\n            t = t / (e * p - 0.5 * (p + 1.0) * t / p);  // Halley\n        }\n        w = w - t;\n        // UPSTREAM\'S RULE IS 10 * eps * max(|w|, 1/(|p| e^w)). The second\n        // term is DROPPED -- see the header and mirror_lambert. It makes the\n        // tolerance O(1) once w is very negative, and the loop then stops one\n        // iteration early with w wrong in the third decimal.\n        let tol = 10.0 * PETIR_LAMBERT_EPS * abs(w);\n        if (abs(t) < tol) {\n            return w;\n        }\n    }\n    return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n}\n\n// The principal branch W_0(x), for x >= -1/e. NaN below that -- upstream\n// returns -1.0 with GSL_EDOM, and a caller of its natural-prototype form\n// cannot tell that from an answer. See mirror_lambert.\nfn petir_lambert_w0(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    let q = x + PETIR_LAMBERT_ONE_OVER_E;\n    if (x == 0.0) { return 0.0; }\n    if (q < 0.0)  { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (q == 0.0) { return -1.0; }\n    if (q < 1.0e-3) { return petir_lambert_series(sqrt(q)); }\n    var w: f32;\n    if (x < 1.0) {\n        let p = sqrt(2.0 * PETIR_LAMBERT_E * q);\n        w = -1.0 + p * (1.0 + p * (-1.0 / 3.0 + p * 11.0 / 72.0));\n    } else {\n        w = log(x);\n        if (x > 3.0) { w = w - log(w); }\n    }\n    return petir_lambert_halley(x, w, 10);\n}\n\n// The secondary real branch W_{-1}(x), for -1/e <= x < 0. Delegates to W_0\n// for x > 0, which is upstream\'s behaviour -- there is no second real branch\n// there. x == 0 returns 0 by the same convention, although the true limit\n// along this branch is -inf.\nfn petir_lambert_wm1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x > 0.0)  { return petir_lambert_w0(x); }\n    if (x == 0.0) { return 0.0; }\n    let q = x + PETIR_LAMBERT_ONE_OVER_E;\n    if (q < 0.0) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    var w: f32;\n    if (x < -1.0e-6) {\n        let v = petir_lambert_series(-sqrt(q));\n        if (q < 3.0e-3) { return v; }\n        w = v;\n    } else {\n        let l1 = log(-x);\n        let l2 = log(-l1);\n        w = l1 - l2 + l2 / l1;\n    }\n    return petir_lambert_halley(x, w, 32);\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `CLAUSEN`

GSL's Clausen function `Cl_2`, ported from `specfunc/clausen.c` by way of
[`crate::specfunc::clausen`].

**The argument reduction is redesigned for `f32`, not transcribed:** the
`f64` three-way split of `2 pi` leaves no mantissa room for the period
count, so this uses an eight-bit head — taken from `clausen.c`'s own
reflection constants. See [`mirror_clausen`], and note that the usable
range ends about two decades below the refusal.

```rust
pub const CLAUSEN: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::clausen` and\n// `petir::specfunc::trig`, which port GSL 2.8\'s specfunc/clausen.c and the\n// angle reductions in specfunc/trig.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman.\n//\n// Cl_2(x) = -integral_0^x ln|2 sin(t/2)| dt = sum_{k>=1} sin(kx)/k^2.\n// Odd, 2pi-periodic, zero at 0 and pi, maximum 1.0149416 at pi/3. It is the\n// imaginary part of Li_2(e^{ix}), which makes it dilog.wgsl\'s trigonometric\n// sibling.\n//\n// THE ARGUMENT REDUCTION IS REDESIGNED FOR f32, NOT TRANSCRIBED.\n//\n// GSL splits 2pi into three f64 pieces P1+P2+P3 so that each y*Pk subtraction\n// is exact. Those constants do not carry over: P1 has about 30 significant\n// bits, which leaves no room in an f32 mantissa for the period count y. So\n// this uses a COARSER HEAD -- and takes it from upstream itself, because\n// clausen.c already carries exactly such a split for its own pi-reflection\n// step:\n//\n//     p0 = 6.28125                    (201/32 -- EIGHT significant bits)\n//     p1 = 0.19353071795864769253e-2\n//\n// plus a third piece so the three sum to 2pi to f64 accuracy. An 8-bit head\n// leaves 16 bits for y, i.e. exact subtraction out to about 65000 periods.\n//\n// MEASURED, worst |sin(reduce(theta)) - sin(theta mod 2pi)| over 2000 probes\n// per decade, against a naive single-f32 2pi reduction:\n//\n//   theta            split      naive      ratio   theta\'s own ulp\n//   1e0              3.937e-09  1.748e-07     44   1.192e-07\n//   1e2              2.384e-07  4.682e-05    196   7.629e-06\n//   1e3              3.052e-07  4.091e-04   1341   6.104e-05\n//   1e4              9.783e-07  5.350e-03   5468   9.766e-04\n//   1e5              7.234e-06  2.897e-02   4004   7.812e-03\n//   2.6e5 .. 5.2e5   7.774e-06  2.893e-02  ~3700   --\n//\n// THE SPLIT HOLDS NEAR 8e-06 ALL THE WAY TO THE REFUSAL, three to four\n// thousand times better than the naive form, which instead tracks theta\'s\n// own ulp. There is no collapse inside the usable range.\n//\n// That is not luck. An eight-bit head keeps y*P0 exact while y fits in\n// sixteen bits, i.e. out to 65536 periods -- 4.12e5 in theta, against a\n// refusal at 5.24e5. THE HEAD WIDTH AND THE CUT ARE MATCHED to within a\n// factor of 1.3, and the small rise from 7.23e-06 to 7.77e-06 in the last\n// row is that limit starting to bite.\n//\n// THE REFUSAL IS AT 0.0625/f32::EPSILON = 524288, the correct f32 analogue of\n// upstream\'s threshold -- a PRECISION constant, retargeted, unlike\n// airy.wgsl\'s range guard which is kept. Here, unusually, the cut and the\n// usable range nearly coincide; in the f64 module they are seven decades\n// apart.\n//\n// A note on how this was measured: |reduce(theta) - (theta mod 2pi)| is the\n// obvious instrument and it is WRONG -- at a period boundary the reduced\n// value jumps between 0 and 2pi, so a probe landing either side reports an\n// error of 2pi when nothing is amiss. The comparison goes through sin, which\n// is continuous there.\n\nconst PETIR_CLAUSEN_P0: f32 = 6.28125;        // 201/32, 8 significant bits\nconst PETIR_CLAUSEN_P1: f32 = 1.9353072e-3;\nconst PETIR_CLAUSEN_P2: f32 = 1.0253132e-11;\nconst PETIR_CLAUSEN_TWO_PI: f32 = 6.2831855;  // = P0 + P1 + P2 in f32\nconst PETIR_CLAUSEN_PI: f32 = 3.1415927;\n// 0.0625 / f32::EPSILON -- upstream\'s threshold, retargeted.\nconst PETIR_CLAUSEN_LOSS_CUT: f32 = 524288.0;\n// pi * sqrt(f32::EPSILON) -- the small-argument cut, also retargeted.\nconst PETIR_CLAUSEN_X_CUT: f32 = 1.0846882e-3;\n\n// GSL\'s `aclaus_data` at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 9 of the 15 stored,\n// where `f64` evaluates 15.\nfn petir_clausen_cheb(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 9>(\n        2.1426945, 0.07233243, 0.0010164248, 3.2452503e-5, 1.3331519e-6, 6.2132406e-8,\n        3.1300413e-9, 1.6635723e-10, 9.196593e-12,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 8; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// Reduce theta >= 0 to [0, 2pi) with the coarse-head split. NaN past the\n// loss cut -- see the header, and note the usable range is far below it.\nfn petir_clausen_reduce(theta: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(theta == theta) || abs(theta) > PETIR_CLAUSEN_LOSS_CUT) {\n        return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n    }\n    let y = floor(theta / PETIR_CLAUSEN_TWO_PI);\n    var r = ((theta - y * PETIR_CLAUSEN_P0) - y * PETIR_CLAUSEN_P1) - y * PETIR_CLAUSEN_P2;\n    if (r > PETIR_CLAUSEN_TWO_PI) {\n        r = ((r - PETIR_CLAUSEN_P0) - PETIR_CLAUSEN_P1) - PETIR_CLAUSEN_P2;\n    } else if (r < 0.0) {\n        r = ((r + PETIR_CLAUSEN_P0) + PETIR_CLAUSEN_P1) + PETIR_CLAUSEN_P2;\n    }\n    return r;\n}\n\n// Cl_2(x) for all real x. NaN past the reduction\'s loss cut, and for NaN.\nfn petir_clausen(x_in: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x_in == x_in)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    var x = x_in;\n    var sgn = 1.0;\n    if (x < 0.0) { x = -x; sgn = -1.0; }\n\n    x = petir_clausen_reduce(x);\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n\n    if (x > PETIR_CLAUSEN_PI) {\n        // Upstream\'s own simulated extra precision for pi - x: the same two\n        // constants the reduction above is built from.\n        x = (PETIR_CLAUSEN_P0 - x) + PETIR_CLAUSEN_P1;\n        sgn = -sgn;\n    }\n\n    var val: f32;\n    if (x == 0.0) {\n        val = 0.0;\n    } else if (x < PETIR_CLAUSEN_X_CUT) {\n        // Cl_2(x) ~ x(1 - ln x). Not an optimisation: the Chebyshev branch\n        // forms a difference of two large quantities there.\n        val = x * (1.0 - log(x));\n    } else {\n        let t = 2.0 * (x * x / (PETIR_CLAUSEN_PI * PETIR_CLAUSEN_PI) - 0.5);\n        val = x * (petir_clausen_cheb(t) - log(x));\n    }\n    return sgn * val;\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `TRANSPORT`

GSL's transport integrals `J(n, x)` for `n = 2 ..= 5`, ported from
`specfunc/transport.c` by way of [`crate::specfunc::transport`].

**Three machine constants are retargeted**, all of them precision
constants; `GSL_LOG_DBL_EPSILON` is load-bearing twice over, setting both
the number of exponential images summed and the point at which the tail is
discarded. See [`mirror_transport`].

```rust
pub const TRANSPORT: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::transport`, which ports\n// GSL 2.8\'s specfunc/transport.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman.\n//\n// J(n, x) = integral_0^x t^n e^t / (e^t - 1)^2 dt, for n = 2..5. The\n// Bloch-Gruneisen transport integrals: J(2) in the electrical and thermal\n// conductivity of a metal, J(4) and J(5) in phonon-limited resistivity. Same\n// physics as debye.wgsl one derivative apart -- the integrand is the\n// derivative of the Bose-Einstein occupation times t^n.\n//\n// EVERY COEFFICIENT WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the f64 module -- 72\n// literals across four Chebyshev series -- and the same script emits\n// `wgsl::mirror_transport`, so the shader and its CPU mirror cannot disagree\n// about a constant.\n//\n// THREE MACHINE CONSTANTS ARE RETARGETED, and all three are PRECISION\n// constants rather than range guards, so by the taxonomy in\n// docs/wgsl-coverage.md they must be. Measured consequences in\n// mirror_transport.\n//\n//   GSL_LOG_DBL_EPSILON   -36.0437  ->  -15.942385   (ln f32::EPSILON)\n//   3 sqrt(DBL_EPSILON)    4.47e-08 ->    1.0358e-3  (3 sqrt f32::EPSILON)\n//   2 / DBL_EPSILON        9.01e+15 ->    1.6777e+7  (2 / f32::EPSILON)\n//\n// A PREDICTION RECORDED AND REFUTED. The first constant was expected to be\n// load-bearing twice over -- it sets `numexp`, the number of exponential\n// images summed in the tail, AND it is the threshold below which the tail is\n// discarded and J(n, inf) returned exactly. Measured, only the first is real:\n//\n//   x      numexp with f32 log-eps   with GSL\'s f64 value\n//   5                4                       8\n//   10               2                       4\n//   16               1                       3\n//   30               1                       2\n//\n//   saturation point   f32 log-eps   f64 log-eps\n//   J(2)                 22.25         22.25\n//   J(3)                 25.05         25.05\n//   J(4)                 27.25         27.25\n//   J(5)                 29.60         29.60\n//\n//   worst relative vs the f64 module, over x in (0, 75]:\n//     shipped  1.3633715693879367e-06\n//     f64      1.3633715693879367e-06   <- identical to the last digit\n//\n// The saturation point does not move, because `vinf - exp(t)` collapses to\n// `vinf` as soon as exp(t) falls below half an ulp of vinf -- which happens\n// well before t reaches -36. THE ARITHMETIC ENFORCES THE GUARD BEFORE THE\n// GUARD DOES, exactly as airy.wgsl\'s overflow threshold is enforced by f32\'s\n// own exp overflow.\n//\n// So retargeting here is CORRECT but its only measurable effect is that the\n// tail sums HALF AS MANY IMAGES for the same answer. Worth doing; not worth\n// claiming an accuracy benefit for.\n\nconst PETIR_TRANSPORT_LOG_EPS: f32 = -15.942385;\nconst PETIR_TRANSPORT_SMALL_CUT: f32 = 1.0358009e-3;\nconst PETIR_TRANSPORT_TWO_OVER_EPS: f32 = 16777216.0;\n\n// GSL\'s transport2_cs, 18 coefficients.\nfn petir_transport_cheb2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 18>(\n        1.6717604398727417, -0.1477353572845459, 0.014821382239460945, -0.0014195330440998077,\n        0.00013065413804724813, -1.1715579603333026e-05, 1.0333498039472033e-06,\n        -9.019112923169814e-08, 7.817717140312652e-09, -6.744565461680452e-10,\n        5.799464034006441e-11, -4.9747619218498684e-12, 4.259609971603989e-13,\n        -3.6421999991724865e-14, 3.110999972851013e-15, -2.6500000149068143e-16,\n        2.3000000123137025e-17, -1.89999995262919e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 17; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s transport3_cs, 18 coefficients.\nfn petir_transport_cheb3(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 18>(\n        0.7620125412940979, -0.1056743860244751, 0.01197780855000019, -0.001214401563629508,\n        0.00011550997442100197, -1.0581598871794995e-05, 9.474663329456234e-07,\n        -8.362211900703187e-08, 7.310910099533885e-09, -6.350595049831043e-10,\n        5.4911828556436504e-11, -4.732139593371931e-12, 4.067695074001787e-13,\n        -3.4897100129310105e-14, 2.9892000231676336e-15, -2.5600001172830847e-16,\n        2.1900000455312983e-17, -1.89999995262919e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 17; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s transport4_cs, 18 coefficients.\nfn petir_transport_cheb4(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 18>(\n        0.48075708746910095, -0.08175379037857056, 0.010027006268501282,\n        -0.0010599339148029685, 0.00010345062764827162, -9.64427090366371e-06,\n        8.745544164412422e-07, -7.793212120077442e-08, 6.864988577603981e-09,\n        -5.999570840131696e-10, 5.213662487846271e-11, -4.511838385540257e-12,\n        3.89215894756878e-13, -3.349360041702762e-14, 2.876700071728633e-15,\n        -2.466999870141503e-16, 2.1099999343327223e-17, -1.800000020426123e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 17; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s transport5_cs, 18 coefficients.\nfn petir_transport_cheb5(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 18>(\n        0.347777783870697, -0.06645698845386505, 0.008611072786152363, -0.0009396682144142687,\n        9.363247954752296e-05, -8.857132343109697e-06, 8.119150152197108e-07,\n        -7.29576541402821e-08, 6.469714541879057e-09, -5.68490310381975e-10,\n        4.9625598769198476e-11, -4.3109400597873826e-12, 3.7309998840440173e-13,\n        -3.2197999149698175e-14, 2.7720000231844233e-15, -2.3800000573378295e-16,\n        2.0999999824714462e-17, -1.800000020426123e-18,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 17; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\nfn petir_transport_cheb(n: u32, x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (n == 2u) { return petir_transport_cheb2(x); }\n    if (n == 3u) { return petir_transport_cheb3(x); }\n    if (n == 4u) { return petir_transport_cheb4(x); }\n    if (n == 5u) { return petir_transport_cheb5(x); }\n    return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n}\n\n// J(n, inf) = n! zeta(n).\nfn petir_transport_vinf(n: u32) -> f32 {\n    if (n == 2u) { return 3.2898681; }\n    if (n == 3u) { return 7.2123413; }\n    if (n == 4u) { return 25.975758; }\n    if (n == 5u) { return 124.43133; }\n    return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u);\n}\n\n// Upstream\'s transport_sumexp: the sum over numexp exponential images that\n// carries the large-x tail. The inner loop builds an asymptotic series in\n// 1/(rk x) to `order` terms; the outer accumulates them Horner-wise in t.\nfn petir_transport_sumexp(numexp: u32, order: u32, t: f32, x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var rk = f32(numexp);\n    var out = 0.0;\n    for (var k: u32 = 1u; k <= numexp; k = k + 1u) {\n        var sum2 = 1.0;\n        let xk = 1.0 / (rk * x);\n        var xk1 = 1.0;\n        for (var j: u32 = 1u; j <= order; j = j + 1u) {\n            sum2 = sum2 * xk1 * xk + 1.0;\n            xk1 = xk1 + 1.0;\n        }\n        out = out * t;\n        out = out + sum2;\n        rk = rk - 1.0;\n    }\n    return out;\n}\n\n// J(n, x) for n in 2..=5. NaN for x < 0, for NaN, and for an untabulated\n// order.\nfn petir_transport(n: u32, x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (n < 2u || n > 5u) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (!(x >= 0.0)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    let nf = f32(n);\n\n    // x^{n-1}, shared by the two small branches.\n    var p = 1.0;\n    for (var k: u32 = 1u; k < n; k = k + 1u) { p = p * x; }\n\n    if (x < PETIR_TRANSPORT_SMALL_CUT) {\n        return p / (nf - 1.0);\n    }\n    if (x <= 4.0) {\n        // Upstream writes (x^2/8 - 0.5) - 0.5, not x^2/8 - 1.0: the two\n        // differ in the last bit near zero, and the grouping is kept.\n        let t = (x * x / 8.0 - 0.5) - 0.5;\n        return p * petir_transport_cheb(n, t);\n    }\n\n    // Past 4: the limit MINUS the tail, not further integration.\n    var t: f32;\n    if (x < -PETIR_TRANSPORT_LOG_EPS) {\n        let numexp = u32((-PETIR_TRANSPORT_LOG_EPS) / x) + 1u;\n        let s = petir_transport_sumexp(numexp, n, exp(-x), x);\n        t = nf * log(x) - x + log(s);\n    } else if (x < PETIR_TRANSPORT_TWO_OVER_EPS) {\n        let s = petir_transport_sumexp(1u, n, 1.0, x);\n        t = nf * log(x) - x + log(s);\n    } else {\n        t = nf * log(x) - x;\n    }\n\n    let vinf = petir_transport_vinf(n);\n    if (t < PETIR_TRANSPORT_LOG_EPS) {\n        return vinf;\n    }\n    return vinf - exp(t);\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `ATANINT`

GSL's inverse-tangent integral `Ti_2`, ported from `specfunc/atanint.c`
by way of [`crate::specfunc::atanint`].

One Chebyshev table evaluated at reciprocal arguments either side of
`|x| = 1`. **The large cut is retargeted and reshapes the domain** — see
[`mirror_atanint`].

```rust
pub const ATANINT: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::atanint`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/atanint.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman.\n//\n// Ti_2(x) = integral_0^x arctan(t)/t dt = sum (-1)^k x^{2k+1}/(2k+1)^2.\n// Odd, unbounded only logarithmically, and Ti_2(1) is Catalan\'s constant --\n// which it shares with clausen.wgsl, its even counterpart.\n//\n// EVERY COEFFICIENT WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the f64 module, whose own\n// table is audited bit-for-bit against GSL\'s source.\n//\n// ONE TABLE, TWO BRANCHES, RECIPROCAL ARGUMENTS. For |x| <= 1 the series is\n// evaluated at 2(x^2 - 1/2); above 1 at 2(1/x^2 - 1/2), combined with\n// (pi/2) ln|x|. That is the Landen-type reflection\n// Ti_2(x) - Ti_2(1/x) = (pi/2) ln x built into the branch structure rather\n// than applied on top, so satisfying it inside the branch is close to a\n// tautology -- what is worth testing is that the branches JOIN.\n//\n// TWO MACHINE CONSTANTS ARE RETARGETED, both precision constants, per the\n// taxonomy in docs/wgsl-coverage.md:\n//\n//   0.5 sqrt(DBL_EPSILON)   7.45e-09  ->  1.7263349e-4\n//   1 / sqrt(DBL_EPSILON)   6.71e+07  ->  2896.3093\n//\n// A PREDICTION RECORDED AND REFUTED. The large cut was expected to RESHAPE\n// THE DOMAIN: above it the series at 1/x^2 has collapsed and the answer is\n// (pi/2) ln|x| + 1/x, and in f32 that arrives 23170 times sooner than in f64,\n// so a far larger share of the domain takes the closed form -- a change in\n// WHICH CODE RUNS.\n//\n// It changes which code runs and NOTHING ELSE. Over 4000 probes spanning the\n// whole disputed window, 2896.3 to 6.711e+07:\n//\n//   answers that differ                    0 of 4000   (bit-identical)\n//   worst rel vs f64, shipped cut          1.594855996429876e-07\n//   worst rel vs f64, GSL\'s f64 cut        1.594855996429876e-07\n//\n// AND THE REASON IS NOT ROUNDING, which two drafts of this note claimed. The\n// series argument 2(1/x^2 - 1/2) never reaches exactly -1 near the cut:\n// -0.99999976 at x = 2900, still -0.99999994 at x = 6000, because the f32\n// spacing just below 0.5 is half that just above. What actually makes the\n// branches agree is that the series enters as cheb(t)/|x| against a\n// (pi/2) ln|x| term that dominates, and the gap between cheb(t) and cheb(-1)\n// divided by |x| falls BELOW ONE ULP of that sum. The series is not\n// collapsing; its variation is being rounded away by the addition.\n//\n// So retargeting is correct and its only effect is that the closed-form\n// branch skips a 21-term Clenshaw spent on a foregone conclusion -- the same\n// WORK-ONLY category as transport.wgsl, established here by bit equality\n// rather than by a bound.\n\nconst PETIR_ATANINT_SMALL_CUT: f32 = 1.7263349e-4;\nconst PETIR_ATANINT_LARGE_CUT: f32 = 2896.3093;\nconst PETIR_ATANINT_PI_2: f32 = 1.5707964;\n\n// GSL\'s `atanint_data` at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 11 of the 21 stored,\n// where `f64` evaluates 21.\nfn petir_atanint_cheb(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 11>(\n        1.9104036092758179, -0.041763514280319214, 0.002753925509750843,\n        -0.00025051808916032314, 2.666981345100794e-05, -3.118905169685604e-06,\n        3.8833852045172534e-07, -5.0572744214605336e-08, 6.812252983934286e-09,\n        -9.421255997565936e-10, 1.3307878410362406e-10,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 10; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// Ti_2(x) for all real x. NaN propagates; there is no domain error and no\n// overflow.\nfn petir_atanint(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x == x)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    let ax = abs(x);\n    var sgn = 1.0;\n    if (x < 0.0) { sgn = -1.0; }\n\n    if (ax == 0.0) { return 0.0; }\n    if (ax < PETIR_ATANINT_SMALL_CUT) {\n        // Ti_2(x) ~ x, the series\' first term.\n        return x;\n    }\n    if (ax <= 1.0) {\n        return x * petir_atanint_cheb(2.0 * (x * x - 0.5));\n    }\n    if (ax < PETIR_ATANINT_LARGE_CUT) {\n        let t = 2.0 * (1.0 / (x * x) - 0.5);\n        return sgn * (PETIR_ATANINT_PI_2 * log(ax) + petir_atanint_cheb(t) / ax);\n    }\n    // The series at 1/x^2 has collapsed to its leading term, 1.\n    return sgn * (PETIR_ATANINT_PI_2 * log(ax) + 1.0 / ax);\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `SYNCHROTRON`

GSL's synchrotron radiation functions `S_1` and `S_2`, ported from
`specfunc/synchrotron.c` by way of [`crate::specfunc::synchrotron`].

**Its underflow guard is dead code in `f64` and load-bearing in `f32`** —
the one constant so far whose category depends on the width. See
[`mirror_synchrotron`].

```rust
pub const SYNCHROTRON: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::synchrotron`, which ports\n// GSL 2.8\'s specfunc/synchrotron.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman; small-argument correction terms\n//   by Brian Gough.\n//\n// S_1(x) = x integral_x^inf K_{5/3}(t) dt   -- total synchrotron power\n// S_2(x) = x K_{2/3}(x)                     -- the polarised difference\n//\n// Both rise like x^{1/3} and fall like sqrt(pi x / 2) e^{-x}: a spectrum with\n// one broad peak. x is frequency in units of the critical frequency.\n//\n// EVERY COEFFICIENT WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the f64 module -- 91\n// literals across six Chebyshev series -- and the same script emits\n// `wgsl::mirror_synchrotron`, so the shader and its CPU mirror cannot\n// disagree about a constant.\n//\n// ONE MACHINE CONSTANT IS RETARGETED AND ONE IS DELIBERATELY KEPT, and\n// telling them apart took a measurement that reversed the first answer.\n//\n//   2 sqrt(2) sqrt(DBL_EPSILON)   4.21e-08 -> 0.0009765625 (exactly 2^-10)\n//       A PRECISION constant. Between those the function is\n// still returning representable denormals -- 5.65e-43 just below the cut, and\n// f32 holds down to 1.4e-45. NaN for x < 0 and for NaN; 0 past the underflow cut.\nfn petir_synchrotron_1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= 0.0)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x < PETIR_SYNCH_SMALL_CUT) {\n        // Brian Gough\'s first-order correction to the x^{1/3} series.\n        let z = pow(x, 1.0 / 3.0);\n        return 2.1495283 * z * (1.0 - 0.84381276 * z * z);\n    }\n    if (x <= 4.0) {\n        let px = pow(x, 1.0 / 3.0);\n        let t = x * x / 8.0 - 1.0;\n        return px * petir_synch_cheb_synch1(t)\n             - petir_synch_pow_int(px, 11u) * petir_synch_cheb_synch2(t)\n             - PETIR_SYNCH_PI_OVER_SQRT3 * x;\n    }\n    if (x < PETIR_SYNCH_UNDERFLOW_CUT) {\n        let t = (12.0 - x) / (x + 4.0);\n        return sqrt(x) * petir_synch_cheb_synch1a(t) * exp(PETIR_SYNCH_LOG_SQRT_PI_2 - x);\n    }\n    // Upstream\'s UNDERFLOW_ERROR. #### Constant `FERMI_DIRAC`
```

GSL's complete Fermi-Dirac integrals `F_j` at the seven fixed indices,
ported from `specfunc/fermi_dirac.c` by way of
[`crate::specfunc::fermi_dirac`].

**The largest table set here** — 22 Chebyshev series, 483 coefficients —
and the one shader that deliberately **corrects** an upstream constant's
formula rather than retargeting its value. See [`mirror_fermi_dirac`].

```rust
pub const FERMI_DIRAC: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::fermi_dirac`, which ports\n// GSL 2.8\'s specfunc/fermi_dirac.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman.\n//   Branch structure and small-argument series after Goano, ACM TOMS 21\n//   (1995) 221-232; the Chebyshev fits are Jungman\'s.\n//\n//   F_j(x) = (1/Gamma(j+1)) integral_0^inf t^j / (e^{t-x} + 1) dt\n//\n// the occupation integrals of a Fermi gas. x is the reduced chemical\n// potential mu/kT. Seven fixed indices: j = -1, -1/2, 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2, 2.\n//\n// EVERY COEFFICIENT WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the f64 module -- 483\n// literals across 22 Chebyshev series, the largest table set in this module\n// -- and the same script emits `wgsl::mirror_fermi_dirac`, so the shader and\n// its CPU mirror cannot disagree about a constant.\n//\n// ============================================================================\n// THE SERIES ACCELERATION IS NOT HERE, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT\n// ============================================================================\n//\n// GSL\'s fd_asymp calls fd_neg, which can run a Levin u-transform over two\n// 101-element work arrays. That was recorded as the blocker for this shader:\n// 202 f32 of function-local storage is real, and psi_zeta.wgsl already\n// declined a single 101-element local array for the same reason.\n//\n// It is never reached. fd_neg is called only from fd_asymp, which runs only\n// at x >= 30, so fd_neg always sees -x <= -30 and always takes its simple\n// alternating series instead. Proven by instrumentation in the f64 module,\n// not by reading branch conditions.\n//\n// Three consequences, all measured, and together they remove every obstacle:\n//\n//   1. NO SCRATCH MEMORY. The acceleration is unreachable, so it is absent.\n//\n//   2. THE REFLECTION TERM IS EXACTLY ZERO. fd_asymp computes\n//      cos(j*pi) * F_j(-x) + 2 * seqn * exp(...), and cos(j*pi) vanishes\n//      identically for j = -1/2, 1/2, 3/2 -- the only indices that reach it.\n//      Upstream carries the term because its j is a runtime parameter; ours\n//      is not. Measured contribution before dropping: 1e-31 to 1e-64\n//      relative. So fd_neg is not transcribed at all.\n//\n//   3. lnGamma(j+2) IS A COMPILE-TIME CONSTANT for each of the three, so\n//      gamma.wgsl is not a dependency. Likewise eta(2n) is a nine-entry\n//      table rather than a call into psi_zeta.wgsl.\n//\n// ============================================================================\n// FOUR MACHINE CONSTANTS, AND ONE OF THEM IS UPSTREAM\'S MISTAKE\n// ============================================================================\n//\n//   GSL_DBL_EPSILON, series break    2.22e-16 -> 1.1920929e-7   PRECISION,\n//                                                               retargeted\n//\n//   GSL_LOG_DBL_MIN, underflow       -708.396 -> KEPT           RANGE GUARD\n//       Same call as synchrotron.wgsl\'s: a bound derived from the exponent\n//       range is enforced by the arithmetic anyway, and retargeting it to\n//       f32\'s -87.3365 would discard representable denormals, since\n//       F_j(x) ~ e^x and e^{-90} = 8.2e-40 is a perfectly good f32.\n//\n//   1/GSL_SQRT_DBL_EPSILON, F_1      6.711e7  -> 2896.3093      PRECISION,\n//                                                               retargeted\n//       Past this, F_1 drops its 60/x Chebyshev fit for the pure degenerate\n//       limit x^2/2. What the fit carries is the Sommerfeld correction\n//       1 + (pi^2/3)/x^2, so the cut belongs where that falls below eps.\n//       At upstream\'s value the correction is 6.7e-16, about 3 f64 eps; at\n//       1/sqrt(f32 eps) it is 3.9e-07, about 3 f32 eps.
```
