Nine is generous:\n// f32 needs three at x = 30 and two past x = 100, where f64 needs seventeen.\nfn petir_fd_eta(n: u32) -> f32 {\n    var e = array<f32, 9>(\n        0.82246703, 0.94703283, 0.98555109, 0.99623300, 0.99903951,\n        0.99975769, 0.99993917, 0.99998476, 0.99999619,\n    );\n    if (n < 1u || n > 9u) { return 1.0; }\n    return e[n - 1u];\n}\n\n// Goano\'s alternating series (6) for an INTEGER index, with the ratio raised\n// to the integer power p = j + 1: sum_{n>=1} (-1)^{n-1} e^{nx} / n^{j+1},\n// written as a running product so no power is evaluated per term.\nfn petir_fd_series(x: f32, p: u32) -> f32 {\n    let ex = exp(x);\n    var term = ex;\n    var sum = term;\n    for (var n: u32 = 2u; n < 100u; n = n + 1u) {\n        let rat = (f32(n) - 1.0) / f32(n);\n        var r = 1.0;\n        for (var k: u32 = 0u; k < p; k = k + 1u) { r = r * rat; }\n        term = term * (-ex) * r;\n        sum = sum + term;\n        if (abs(term / sum) < PETIR_FD_EPS) { break; }\n    }\n    return sum;\n}\n\n// The same series for a HALF-INTEGER index: the ratio carries a sqrt, and\n// `whole` supplies the remaining integer part -- 0 for -1/2, 1 for 1/2,\n// 2 for 3/2, matching upstream\'s sqrt(rat), rat*sqrt(rat), rat*rat*sqrt(rat).\nfn petir_fd_series_half(x: f32, whole: u32) -> f32 {\n    let ex = exp(x);\n    var term = ex;\n    var sum = term;\n    for (var n: u32 = 2u; n < 200u; n = n + 1u) {\n        let rat = (f32(n) - 1.0) / f32(n);\n        var r = sqrt(rat);\n        for (var k: u32 = 0u; k < whole; k = k + 1u) { r = r * rat; }\n        term = term * (-ex) * r;\n        sum = sum + term;\n        if (abs(term / sum) < PETIR_FD_EPS) { break; }\n    }\n    return sum;\n}\n\n// GSL\'s fd_asymp for a half-integer j, WITHOUT the reflection term, which is\n// identically zero here because cos(j*pi) vanishes for j = -1/2, 1/2, 3/2.\n// `lg` is ln Gamma(j+2), a constant at each of the three.\nfn petir_fd_asymp(j: f32, lg: f32, x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var seqn = 0.5;\n    let xm2 = (1.0 / x) / x;\n    var xgam = 1.0;\n    var add = 3.4028235e38;\n    for (var n: u32 = 1u; n <= 9u; n = n + 1u) {\n        let add_previous = add;\n        xgam = xgam * xm2 * (j + 1.0 - (2.0 * f32(n) - 2.0)) * (j + 1.0 - (2.0 * f32(n) - 1.0));\n        add = petir_fd_eta(n) * xgam;\n        // j is never an integer here, so the series is genuinely asymptotic\n        // and must be truncated at its smallest term.\n        if (abs(add) > abs(add_previous)) { break; }\n        if (abs(add / seqn) < PETIR_FD_EPS) { break; }\n        seqn = seqn + add;\n    }\n    return 2.0 * seqn * exp((j + 1.0) * log(x) - lg);\n}\n\n// F_{-1}(x) = e^x/(1+e^x), the Fermi occupation function. Bounded by 1.\nfn petir_fd_m1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= PETIR_FD_LOG_MIN)) {\n        if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if (x < 0.0) {\n        // So the exponential evaluated is the small one.\n        let ex = exp(x);\n        return ex / (1.0 + ex);\n    }\n    return 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-x));\n}\n\n// F_0(x) = ln(1+e^x). Three pieces so neither limit loses its leading\n// behaviour to cancellation.\nfn petir_fd_0(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= PETIR_FD_LOG_MIN)) {\n        if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if (x < -5.0) {\n        let ex = exp(x);\n        let ser = 1.0 - ex * (0.5 - ex * (1.0 / 3.0 - ex * (0.25 - ex * (0.2 - ex / 6.0))));\n        return ex * ser;\n    }\n    if (x < 10.0) {\n        return log(1.0 + exp(x));\n    }\n    let ex = exp(-x);\n    return x + ex * (1.0 - 0.5 * ex + ex * ex / 3.0 - ex * ex * ex / 4.0);\n}\n\nfn petir_fd_1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= PETIR_FD_LOG_MIN)) {\n        if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if (x < -1.0) { return petir_fd_series(x, 2u); }\n    if (x < 1.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_1_a(x); }\n    if (x < 4.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_1_b(2.0 / 3.0 * (x - 1.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 10.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_1_c(1.0 / 3.0 * (x - 4.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 30.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_1_d(0.1 * x - 2.0) * x * x; }\n    if (x < PETIR_FD_FAR_CUT) { return petir_fd_cheb_1_e(60.0 / x - 1.0) * x * x; }\n    // Upstream\'s OVERFLOW_ERROR bound, GSL_SQRT_DBL_MAX = 1.34e154, IS NOT\n    // REPRESENTABLE as an f32 -- so it is not kept and not retargeted, it\n    // ceases to exist. x*x reaches infinity at ~2.6e19 on its own, which is\n    // the same answer the guard would have given. See the header.\n    return 0.5 * x * x;\n}\n\nfn petir_fd_2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= PETIR_FD_LOG_MIN)) {\n        if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if (x < -1.0) { return petir_fd_series(x, 3u); }\n    if (x < 1.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_2_a(x); }\n    if (x < 4.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_2_b(2.0 / 3.0 * (x - 1.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 10.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_2_c(1.0 / 3.0 * (x - 4.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 30.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_2_d(0.1 * x - 2.0) * x * x * x; }\n    // PETIR_FD_FAR_CUT, not the cube-root analogue -- see the header.\n    if (x < PETIR_FD_FAR_CUT) { return petir_fd_cheb_2_e(60.0 / x - 1.0) * x * x * x; }\n    // GSL_ROOT3_DBL_MAX = 5.64e102 is likewise not an f32; x*x*x reaches\n    // infinity at ~1.4e13 by itself.\n    return x * x * x / 6.0;\n}\n\nfn petir_fd_mhalf(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= PETIR_FD_LOG_MIN)) {\n        if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if (x < -1.0) { return petir_fd_series_half(x, 0u); }\n    if (x < 1.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_mhalf_a(x); }\n    if (x < 4.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_mhalf_b(2.0 / 3.0 * (x - 1.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 10.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_mhalf_c(1.0 / 3.0 * (x - 4.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 30.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_mhalf_d(0.1 * x - 2.0) * sqrt(x); }\n    return petir_fd_asymp(-0.5, PETIR_FD_LG_MHALF, x);\n}\n\nfn petir_fd_half(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= PETIR_FD_LOG_MIN)) {\n        if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if (x < -1.0) { return petir_fd_series_half(x, 1u); }\n    if (x < 1.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_half_a(x); }\n    if (x < 4.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_half_b(2.0 / 3.0 * (x - 1.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 10.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_half_c(1.0 / 3.0 * (x - 4.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 30.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_half_d(0.1 * x - 2.0) * (x * sqrt(x)); }\n    return petir_fd_asymp(0.5, PETIR_FD_LG_HALF, x);\n}\n\nfn petir_fd_3half(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= PETIR_FD_LOG_MIN)) {\n        if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    if (x < -1.0) { return petir_fd_series_half(x, 2u); }\n    if (x < 1.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_3half_a(x); }\n    if (x < 4.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_3half_b(2.0 / 3.0 * (x - 1.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 10.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_3half_c(1.0 / 3.0 * (x - 4.0) - 1.0); }\n    if (x < 30.0) { return petir_fd_cheb_3half_d(0.1 * x - 2.0) * (x * x * sqrt(x)); }\n    return petir_fd_asymp(1.5, PETIR_FD_LG_3HALF, x);\n}\n\n// One dispatcher over the seven indices, in ascending order of j:\n// 0 -> F_{-1}, 1 -> F_{-1/2}, 2 -> F_0, 3 -> F_{1/2}, 4 -> F_1,\n// 5 -> F_{3/2}, 6 -> F_2. Any other `which` gives NaN.\nfn petir_fermi_dirac(which: u32, x: f32) -> f32 {\n    switch (which) {\n        case 0u: { return petir_fd_m1(x); }\n        case 1u: { return petir_fd_mhalf(x); }\n        case 2u: { return petir_fd_0(x); }\n        case 3u: { return petir_fd_half(x); }\n        case 4u: { return petir_fd_1(x); }\n        case 5u: { return petir_fd_3half(x); }\n        case 6u: { return petir_fd_2(x); }\n        default: { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    }\n}\n";

#### Constant `DAWSON`

Dawson's integral `F(x)`, ported from `specfunc/dawson.c` by way of
[`crate::specfunc::dawson`].

**The first shader here to ship GSL's single-precision Chebyshev order**
rather than its `f64` one — 45 coefficients where the `f64` order needs
84. See [`mirror_dawson`].

```rust
pub const DAWSON: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::dawson`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/dawson.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman; the Chebyshev fits come from\n//   SLATEC\'s daws.f by W. Fullerton.\n//\n//   F(x) = e^{-x^2} integral_0^x e^{t^2} dt\n//\n// the odd, bounded companion of erf: it rises to 0.5410442 at x = 0.9241389\n// and decays like 1/(2x). It is what exp(x^2) erf(x) would be if that product\n// did not overflow, and the imaginary part of the Faddeeva function on the\n// real axis.\n//\n// EVERY COEFFICIENT WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the f64 module and the same\n// script emits `wgsl::mirror_dawson`, so the shader and its CPU mirror cannot\n// disagree about a constant.\n//\n// ============================================================================\n// THE FIRST SHADER HERE TO USE GSL\'S SINGLE-PRECISION ORDER\n// ============================================================================\n//\n// GSL\'s cheb_series struct has FIVE fields and the fifth is order_sp -- the\n// order to use in single precision, which GSL_MODE_SINGLE selects inside\n// cheb_eval_mode:\n//\n//   static cheb_series dawa_cs = { dawa_data, 34, /* 74, */ -1, 1, 12 };\n//                                              ^^                    ^^\n//                                          f64 order            order_sp\n//\n// Every earlier shader in this module ships the f64 order. This one ships\n// order_sp, which is upstream\'s own answer for exactly this width -- porting,\n// not inventing a truncation. The cost:\n//\n//   table       stored   f64 uses   order_sp   answer-level cost\n//   daw_data        21         16         10   measured in mirror_dawson\n//   daw2_data       45         33         22\n//   dawa_data       75         35         13\n//\n// 45 coefficients where the f64 order would need 84, and where the raw arrays\n// hold 141. dawa alone falls from 35 to 13.\n//\n// That matters beyond size: debye.wgsl measured that series held as INLINE\n// array<f32, N> literals do not reproduce the CPU bit for bit where\n// storage-buffer coefficients do -- 34/64 against 64/64 -- and every series\n// here is inline. Shortening them is a direct experiment on that.\n//\n// ============================================================================\n// THREE MACHINE CONSTANTS, AND THE THIRD CANNOT BE WRITTEN DOWN\n// ============================================================================\n//\n//   1.225 * SQRT_DBL_EPSILON   1.825e-08 -> 4.2295e-4     PRECISION,\n//                                                         retargeted\n//   1/(sqrt2 * SQRT_DBL_EPS)   4.745e+07 -> 2048.0        PRECISION,\n//                                                         retargeted --\n//       and it lands on exactly 2^11, the same way fermi_dirac\'s small cut\n//       landed on 2^-10: 2^{-1/2} * 2^{23/2} = 2^11 by algebra.\n//\n//   0.1 * GSL_DBL_MAX          1.798e+307 -> DELETED      RANGE GUARD, NOT\n//                                                         REPRESENTABLE\n//       f32::MAX is 3.4e38, so 0.1*DBL_MAX cannot be an f32 at all -- the\n//       same third outcome fermi_dirac.wgsl\'s overflow bounds met. The branch\n//       is removed and 0.5/x is left to underflow on its own, which it does\n//       only past 3.4e38 and into denormals that are perfectly representable.\n//       Deleting the guard therefore GAINS answers here rather than losing\n//       them.\n\n// GSL\'s daw_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 10 of the\n// 21 stored, where f64 uses 16. See the header.\nfn petir_dawson_cheb_daw(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 10>(\n        -0.006351734511554241, -0.2294071465730667, 0.02213050052523613,\n        -0.001549265463836491, 8.49732750793919e-05, -3.828266471828101e-06,\n        1.462854868350405e-07, -4.85198237143436e-09, 1.4214636412379633e-10,\n        -3.728836250188605e-12,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 9; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s daw2_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 22 of the\n// 45 stored, where f64 uses 33. See the header.\nfn petir_dawson_cheb_daw2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 22>(\n        -0.056886542588472366, -0.3181134760379791, 0.20873846113681793,\n        -0.12475410103797913, 0.06786930561065674, -0.03365914523601532,\n        0.015260781161487103, -0.006348371040076017, 0.0024326741695404053,\n        -0.0008621953893452883, 0.0002837657229974866, -8.70575531735085e-05,\n        2.4986849894048646e-05, -6.7319288064027205e-06, 1.7078579048757092e-06,\n        -4.09175498816694e-07, 9.282829438461704e-08, -1.9991404087704723e-08,\n        4.096349037752134e-09, -8.003240847820337e-10, 1.4938503212214016e-10,\n        -2.668799903293717e-11,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 21; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s dawa_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 13 of the\n// 75 stored, where f64 uses 35. See the header.\nfn petir_dawson_cheb_dawa(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 13>(\n        0.016904857009649277, 0.008683252148330212, 0.00024248640693258494,\n        1.2611823876795825e-05, 1.066453364728659e-06, 1.358159806841286e-07,\n        2.1710423681042812e-08, 2.8670104068595492e-09, -1.9013364493947194e-10,\n        -3.097780365557412e-10, -1.0294148866663022e-10, -6.260356382598031e-12,\n        8.563132841699073e-12,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 12; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// 1.225 * sqrt(f32::EPSILON).\nconst PETIR_DAW_XSML: f32 = 4.2295206e-4;\n// 1/(sqrt(2) * sqrt(f32::EPSILON)), exactly 2^11.\nconst PETIR_DAW_XBIG: f32 = 2048.0;\n\n// F(x). NaN propagates; there is no refusal and no overflow.\nfn petir_dawson(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    let y = abs(x);\n    if (y < PETIR_DAW_XSML) { return x; }\n    if (y < 1.0) {\n        // The 0.75 is carried outside the fit so the series has no constant\n        // term to lose precision on, as upstream does.\n        return x * (0.75 + petir_dawson_cheb_daw(2.0 * y * y - 1.0));\n    }\n    if (y < 4.0) {\n        return x * (0.25 + petir_dawson_cheb_daw2(0.125 * y * y - 1.0));\n    }\n    if (y < PETIR_DAW_XBIG) {\n        return (0.5 + petir_dawson_cheb_dawa(32.0 / (y * y) - 1.0)) / x;\n    }\n    // Upstream\'s 0.1 * DBL_MAX underflow guard is not an f32; 0.5/x carries\n    // on into denormals instead. See the header.\n    return 0.5 / x;\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `EXPINT3`

The cubic exponential integral `Ei_3(x)`, ported from
`specfunc/expint3.c` by way of [`crate::specfunc::expint3`].

Carries GSL's single-precision Chebyshev order: 27 coefficients where the
`f64` order needs 47. See [`mirror_expint3`].

```rust
pub const EXPINT3: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::expint3`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/expint3.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman.\n//\n//   Ei_3(x) = integral_0^x e^{-t^3} dt\n//\n// the cubic member of the family whose quadratic member is (sqrt(pi)/2)\n// erf(x). It rises monotonically from the origin to Gamma(4/3) and never\n// exceeds it. x >= 0 only: e^{-t^3} GROWS for negative t, so the restriction\n// is real and not a sign convention.\n//\n// EVERY COEFFICIENT WAS EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the f64 module and the same\n// script emits `wgsl::mirror_expint3`, so the shader and its CPU mirror\n// cannot disagree about a constant. Both tables carry GSL\'S SINGLE-PRECISION\n// ORDER, as dawson.wgsl introduced: 27 coefficients where the f64 order\n// needs 47.\n//\n// THREE MACHINE CONSTANTS, ALL PRECISION, ALL RETARGETED:\n//\n//   1.6 * GSL_ROOT3_DBL_EPSILON     9.689e-06 -> 7.8745065e-3\n//       Below this Ei_3(x) = x to working precision.\n//\n//   (-GSL_LOG_DBL_EPSILON)^(1/3)    3.303261  -> 2.5168138\n//       Past this e^{-x^3} is below one ulp of Gamma(4/3) and the function\n//       is declared equal to it. THE f64 VERSION OF THIS CUT IS EXACTLY\n//       PLACED -- straddling it by one part in 1e13 gives a bit-identical\n//       answer -- which is the standard the retargeted one is measured\n//       against in mirror_expint3.\n//\n//   val_infinity = Gamma(4/3)       0.89297951156924921 -> 0.8929795\n//       Not a threshold; the saturation VALUE. Upstream\'s literal is the\n//       correctly rounded f64, and this is its correctly rounded f32.\n//\n// There is no underflow or overflow guard to decide about: the function is\n// bounded by Gamma(4/3) and its only refusal is the x < 0 domain error.\n\n// GSL\'s expint3_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 16 of the\n// 24 stored, where f64 uses 24. See the header.\nfn petir_expint3_cheb_expint3(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 16>(\n        1.2691984176635742, -0.24884644150733948, 0.08052621781826019,\n        -0.025772733613848686, 0.007599879056215286, -0.002030695555731654,\n        0.0004908345872536302, -0.00010768223728518933, 2.155172660422977e-05,\n        -3.956705313612474e-06, 6.699240771013137e-07, -1.0513218029473137e-07,\n        1.5362580541022908e-08, -2.0990960081235244e-09, 2.6921095908072346e-10,\n        -3.25195252670607e-11,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 15; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s expint3a_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 11 of the\n// 23 stored, where f64 uses 23. See the header.\nfn petir_expint3_cheb_expint3a(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 11>(\n        1.927046537399292, -0.03492935746908188, 0.001450338400900364,\n        -8.925336442189291e-05, 7.054239176795818e-06, -6.671727419416129e-07,\n        7.242675792440423e-08, -8.782582661126526e-09, 1.1672234290216466e-09,\n        -1.676631333769052e-10, 2.5755016175299517e-11,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 10; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// 1.6 * cbrt(f32::EPSILON).\nconst PETIR_E3_SMALL_CUT: f32 = 7.8745065e-3;\n// (-ln(f32::EPSILON))^(1/3).\nconst PETIR_E3_LOG_CUT: f32 = 2.5168138;\n// Gamma(4/3), the value of the integral over the whole half-line.\nconst PETIR_E3_VAL_INFINITY: f32 = 0.8929795;\n\n// Ei_3(x). NaN for x < 0 and for NaN -- upstream\'s DOMAIN_ERROR.\nfn petir_expint_3(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= 0.0)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x < PETIR_E3_SMALL_CUT) { return x; }\n    if (x <= 2.0) {\n        return x * petir_expint3_cheb_expint3(x * x * x / 4.0 - 1.0);\n    }\n    if (x < PETIR_E3_LOG_CUT) {\n        let t = 16.0 / (x * x * x) - 1.0;\n        let s = exp(-(x * x * x)) / (3.0 * x * x);\n        return PETIR_E3_VAL_INFINITY - petir_expint3_cheb_expint3a(t) * s;\n    }\n    return PETIR_E3_VAL_INFINITY;\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `SININT`

The sine and cosine integrals `Si(x)` and `Ci(x)`, ported from
`specfunc/sinint.c` by way of [`crate::specfunc::sinint`].

**Self-contained**: a `2 pi` argument reduction was tried and measured to
be worse on both CPU and GPU, so this shader calls `sin` and `cos`
directly. See [`mirror_sinint`].

```rust
pub const SININT: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::sinint`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/sinint.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman; the two small-argument fits come\n//   from SLATEC\'s si.f and ci.f by W. Fullerton.\n//\n//   Si(x) = integral_0^x sin(t)/t dt\n//   Ci(x) = -integral_x^inf cos(t)/t dt\n//\n// the pair that describes diffraction at a straight edge. Si rises to pi/2\n// with a decaying oscillation; Ci starts at -infinity, crosses zero at\n// x = 0.6165, and oscillates towards zero.\n//\n// SELF-CONTAINED: no argument reduction, and that was MEASURED rather than\n// assumed. See the note at the foot of this header.\n//\n// All six tables carry GSL\'S SINGLE-PRECISION ORDER: 81 coefficients where\n// the f64 order needs 129.\n//\n// FOUR OF THE SIX TABLES BELONG TO f AND g, NOT TO Si AND Ci. Past x = 4,\n//\n//   Si(x) = pi/2 - f(x) cos x - g(x) sin x\n//   Ci(x) =        f(x) sin x - g(x) cos x\n//\n// with f ~ 1/x and g ~ 1/x^2. That is not a convenience: it moves the\n// oscillation entirely into the sin/cos factors, so what gets fitted is\n// smooth and monotone. It also means this kernel\'s accuracy at large x is\n// whatever the device\'s sin and cos can deliver, and nothing this shader\n// does can improve on that.\n//\n// THREE MACHINE CONSTANTS AND TWO DELETED GUARDS:\n//\n//   GSL_SQRT_DBL_EPSILON        1.490e-08 -> 3.4526698e-4   PRECISION\n//   sqrt(50), the f1/f2 split   7.07106781187 -> 7.0710678  BRANCH BOUNDARY,\n//                                                           kept\n//   1/GSL_SQRT_DBL_EPSILON      6.711e+07 -> 2896.3093      PRECISION\n//\n//   1/GSL_DBL_MIN               4.494e+307 -> DELETED       NOT AN f32\n//   1/GSL_SQRT_DBL_MIN          6.704e+153 -> DELETED       NOT AN f32\n//\n// The last two are fermi_dirac.wgsl\'s third outcome again. Here deleting\n// them GAINS answers: the arithmetic reaches the same zeros by itself -- x*x\n// overflows above 1.8e19 so 1/x^2 becomes 0 -- and does so later than either\n// guard\'s f32 analogue would.\n//\n// ============================================================================\n// THE ARGUMENT REDUCTION WAS TRIED AND IS ABSENT ON THE EVIDENCE\n// ============================================================================\n//\n// clausen.wgsl\'s petir_clausen_reduce is the f32 three-way 2*pi split, and\n// reusing it here looked obviously right. Measured, it is worse on both\n// sides, so this shader calls sin and cos directly.\n//\n//   ON THE CPU, against the f64 module, Ci\'s error relative to its own 1/x\n//   envelope over [1e4, 1e5]: 1.955e-07 raw against 1.182e-06 reduced, and\n//   over [1e5, 5.2e5] 1.652e-07 against 7.993e-06. Si is unaffected either\n//   way, because there sin and cos are multiplied by f ~ 1/x against a\n//   leading pi/2; Ci IS f*sin - g*cos, so it carries their error at full\n//   weight. That asymmetry is why Ci is the instrument here.\n//\n//   ON THE DEVICE (llvmpipe, LLVM 20.1.2), sin(x) against f64: within 1e-7\n//   to about x = 1e7, then 7.4e-4 at 1e8. The reduction returns NaN past its\n//   own loss cut of 524288, so above 5.2e5 it is not even available, and\n//   below it it is slightly the worse of the two (0.0357484 against the\n//   correct 0.0357488 at x = 1e5).\n//\n// Both libraries already do a proper multi-word reduction internally. What\n// actually ends the usable range is neither of them: at x = 1e7 one f32 ulp\n// of the ARGUMENT is 1 radian, so sin(x) is not determined by the f32 x at\n// all. See mirror_sinint for the range this kernel is honest over.\n\n// GSL\'s f1_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 11 of the\n// 20 stored, where f64 uses 20. See the header.\nfn petir_sinint_cheb_f1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 11>(\n        -0.11910820007324219, -0.024782314896583557, 0.0011910281609743834,\n        -9.270277223549783e-05, 9.337313713331241e-06, -1.1058288009735406e-06,\n        1.464772054760033e-07, -2.1069450184540983e-08, 3.229349232469758e-09,\n        -5.20652965185775e-10, 8.748789193102624e-11,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 10; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s f2_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 15 of the\n// 29 stored, where f64 uses 29. See the header.\nfn petir_sinint_cheb_f2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 15>(\n        -0.03484092652797699, -0.016684221103787422, 0.0006752901244908571,\n        -5.350666106096469e-05, 6.269342065934325e-06, -9.526638677925803e-07,\n        1.7456292766837578e-07, -3.687954119868664e-08, 8.720268063200365e-09,\n        -2.260197140557807e-09, 6.324624712839011e-10, -1.8889119435261392e-10,\n        5.967746435908694e-11, -1.980443066484927e-11, 6.86413946515696e-12,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 14; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s g1_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 14 of the\n// 21 stored, where f64 uses 21. See the header.\nfn petir_sinint_cheb_g1(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 14>(\n        -0.30405786633491516, -0.056689098477363586, 0.0039046157617121935,\n        -0.00037460759631358087, 4.3543153878999874e-05, -5.741729637520621e-06,\n        8.282552244054386e-07, -1.2782459180016303e-07, 2.079783456565565e-08,\n        -3.531320569294394e-09, 6.210824077257371e-10, -1.1252154763496947e-10,\n        2.0908890938087232e-11, -3.971583045075944e-12,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 13; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s g2_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 21 of the\n// 34 stored, where f64 uses 34. See the header.\nfn petir_sinint_cheb_g2(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 21>(\n        -0.09673293679952621, -0.04520779103040695, 0.0028190005104988813,\n        -0.0002899167884606868, 4.074446769664064e-05, -7.105638360371813e-06,\n        1.453472350476659e-06, -3.364116594184452e-07, 8.597744027838417e-08,\n        -2.3843766072673134e-08, 7.08319047859618e-09, -2.2318067394166974e-09,\n        7.401087520619853e-10, -2.567171197842555e-10, 9.267070444352044e-11,\n        -3.4669329906922286e-11, 1.339505763253701e-11, -5.32907528869031e-12,\n        2.177531158858992e-12, -9.118620572165503e-13, 3.9058640761806263e-13,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 20; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s si_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 10 of the\n// 12 stored, where f64 uses 12. See the header.\nfn petir_sinint_cheb_si(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 10>(\n        -0.131564661860466, -0.2776578664779663, 0.035441406071186066,\n        -0.002563163172453642, 0.0001162365369964391, -3.5904326978197787e-06,\n        8.023421571579092e-08, -1.356299739185829e-09, 1.794407157584832e-11,\n        -1.90838704973266e-13,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 9; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\n// GSL\'s ci_data at its SINGLE-PRECISION order: 10 of the\n// 13 stored, where f64 uses 13. See the header.\nfn petir_sinint_cheb_ci(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    var c = array<f32, 10>(\n        -0.3400428295135498, -1.0330216884613037, 0.19388222694396973,\n        -0.019182603806257248, 0.0011078924871981144, -4.1572344343876466e-05,\n        1.0927852827080642e-06, -2.123285902655425e-08, 3.1733482508400357e-10,\n        -3.761415658110057e-12,\n    );\n    var d = 0.0;\n    var dd = 0.0;\n    let y2 = 2.0 * x;\n    for (var j: i32 = 9; j >= 1; j = j - 1) {\n        let temp = d;\n        d = y2 * d - dd + c[j];\n        dd = temp;\n    }\n    return x * d - dd + 0.5 * c[0];\n}\n\nconst PETIR_SI_SMALL_CUT: f32 = 3.4526698e-4;\n// sqrt(50), upstream\'s rounded decimal, kept verbatim: it is a branch\n// boundary, not a machine constant.\nconst PETIR_SI_XBND: f32 = 7.0710678;\nconst PETIR_SI_XBIG: f32 = 2896.3093;\n\n// (sin x, cos x), straight from the device. A 2*pi reduction was measured\n// and is worse on both CPU and GPU -- see the header.\nfn petir_si_sin_cos(x: f32) -> vec2<f32> {\n    return vec2<f32>(sin(x), cos(x));\n}\n\n// The asymptotic pair (f, g) for x >= 4. Upstream\'s two far-field guards are\n// absent -- neither is an f32; see the header.\nfn petir_si_fg_asymp(x: f32) -> vec2<f32> {\n    let x2 = x * x;\n    if (x <= PETIR_SI_XBND) {\n        let t = (1.0 / x2 - 0.04125) / 0.02125;\n        return vec2<f32>((1.0 + petir_sinint_cheb_f1(t)) / x,\n                         (1.0 + petir_sinint_cheb_g1(t)) / x2);\n    }\n    if (x <= PETIR_SI_XBIG) {\n        let t = 100.0 / x2 - 1.0;\n        return vec2<f32>((1.0 + petir_sinint_cheb_f2(t)) / x,\n                         (1.0 + petir_sinint_cheb_g2(t)) / x2);\n    }\n    return vec2<f32>(1.0 / x, 1.0 / x2);\n}\n\n// Si(x), odd, bounded by 1.8519. NaN propagates.\nfn petir_si(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (x != x) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    let ax = abs(x);\n    if (ax < PETIR_SI_SMALL_CUT) { return x; }\n    if (ax <= 4.0) {\n        // The 0.75 is carried outside the fit, as in GSL.\n        return x * (0.75 + petir_sinint_cheb_si((x * x - 8.0) * 0.125));\n    }\n    let fg = petir_si_fg_asymp(ax);\n    let sc = petir_si_sin_cos(ax);\n    let v = 1.5707964 - fg.x * sc.y - fg.y * sc.x;\n    if (x < 0.0) { return -v; }\n    return v;\n}\n\n// Ci(x). NaN for x <= 0 -- upstream\'s DOMAIN_ERROR, and a real one: Ci has a\n// logarithmic singularity at the origin and a branch cut below it.\nfn petir_ci(x: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x > 0.0)) { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n    if (x <= 4.0) {\n        // ln x carries the singularity; the fit carries the rest.\n        return log(x) - 0.5 + petir_sinint_cheb_ci((x * x - 8.0) * 0.125);\n    }\n    let fg = petir_si_fg_asymp(x);\n    let sc = petir_si_sin_cos(x);\n    return fg.x * sc.x - fg.y * sc.y;\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `ELLINT`

Carlson's symmetric forms and the Legendre elliptic integrals built on
them, ported from `specfunc/ellint.c` by way of
[`crate::specfunc::ellint`].

Provides `petir_ellint_rc` / `rd` / `rf` / `rj`, the four complete
integrals `petir_ellint_kcomp` / `ecomp` / `dcomp` / `pcomp`, the four
incomplete `petir_ellint_f` / `e` / `p` / `d`, and the selector
`petir_ellint_comp(which, k, n)`.

**The second table-free shader here, after [`DILOG`]** — nothing is
fitted, so there is no generator and no table audit. Two parameters are
measured rather than transcribed: `errtol = 0.03` is upstream's own
single-precision value, and the iteration cap is **16 against upstream's
10000**. See [`mirror_ellint`].

```rust
pub const ELLINT: &str = "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only\n//\n// TRANSCRIBED to WGSL (f32) from `petir::specfunc::ellint`, which ports GSL\n// 2.8\'s specfunc/ellint.c.\n//   Copyright (C) 1996-2000 Gerard Jungman.\n//   Algorithms: B. C. Carlson, Numer. Math. 33, 1 (1979); the two near-k=1\n//   series are Abramowitz & Stegun 17.3.34 and 17.3.36.\n//\n//   R_F(x,y,z)   = (1/2) int_0^inf dt / sqrt((t+x)(t+y)(t+z))\n//   R_D(x,y,z)   = (3/2) int_0^inf dt / ((t+z) sqrt((t+x)(t+y)(t+z)))\n//   R_J(x,y,z,p) = (3/2) int_0^inf dt / ((t+p) sqrt((t+x)(t+y)(t+z)))\n//   R_C(x,y)     = R_F(x,y,y)\n//\n// and the Legendre forms F, E, Pi, D follow algebraically.\n//\n// THE SECOND TABLE-FREE SHADER HERE, after dilog.wgsl. Nothing is fitted:\n// the Carlson forms converge by duplication and close with a short\n// polynomial in the deviations. So there is no coefficient array, no\n// order_sp decision, and nothing for the generator that produces the other\n// shaders to do -- this one is written by hand alongside its mirror.\n//\n// ============================================================================\n// TWO DESIGN DECISIONS, BOTH MEASURED\n// ============================================================================\n//\n// 1. errtol = 0.03, WHICH IS UPSTREAM\'S OWN SINGLE-PRECISION VALUE.\n//\n//    GSL\'s routines take a gsl_mode_t and read one thing from it:\n//\n//      GSL_PREC_DOUBLE  ->  errtol 0.001  ->  relative error ~1e-17\n//      otherwise        ->  errtol 0.03   ->  relative error ~2e-08\n//\n//    (upstream\'s own table, in the comment above gsl_sf_ellint_RC_e). This\n//    is the THIRD kind of single-precision parameter GSL supplies, after\n//    cheb_series\'s order_sp and the per-width machine constants -- and the\n//    first that changes the amount of WORK rather than of data. Measured in\n//    f64 over 201 moduli: 8447 duplication steps against Double\'s 14615,\n//    for a 1.309e-11 difference. Five orders below f32\'s epsilon, so it is\n//    free here and halves the iteration count.\n//\n// 2. THE ITERATION CAP IS 16, NOT UPSTREAM\'S 10000.\n//\n//    GSL guards its duplication loops with nmax = 10000. That is a\n//    can\'t-happen bound, not a working one. Measured at errtol 0.03 over the\n//    WHOLE f32-reachable domain -- x and y swept geometrically from\n//    5*FLT_MIN to 0.2*FLT_MAX, 121 x 121 pairs:\n//\n//      R_C   9 steps at worst\n//      R_F   8\n//      R_D   8\n//      R_J  13 in total, including the R_C it calls at every step\n//      a whole Pi(phi,k,n) call: 14 in total\n//\n//    so 16 per loop has room and 10000 is four orders of dead ceiling. On a\n//    GPU that ceiling is not free the way it is on a CPU: a uniform-control\n//    -flow loop bound is what the compiler unrolls against.\n//\n// R_J CALLS R_C INSIDE ITS OWN LOOP, AND THAT IS FINE. WGSL forbids\n// RECURSION, not nested calls, and R_C never calls back. This was recorded\n// as an open question when the f64 module landed and it is not one.\n//\n// f32 DOMAIN BOUNDS, all recomputed from FLT_MIN/FLT_MAX rather than\n// retargeted by hand:\n//   R_F, R_C   lolim 5*FLT_MIN = 5.8775e-38,  uplim 0.2*FLT_MAX = 6.8056e+37\n//   R_D        lolim 2/FLT_MAX^(2/3) = 4.1033e-26,\n//              uplim (0.1*errtol/FLT_MIN)^(2/3) = 4.0235e+23\n//   R_J        lolim (5*FLT_MIN)^(1/3) = 3.8880e-13,\n//              uplim 0.3*(0.2*FLT_MAX)^(1/3) = 1.2248e+12\n\nconst PETIR_ELL_ERRTOL: f32 = 0.03;\nconst PETIR_ELL_NMAX: u32 = 16u;\n\nconst PETIR_ELL_RF_LOLIM: f32 = 5.8774718e-38;\nconst PETIR_ELL_RF_UPLIM: f32 = 6.8056469e37;\nconst PETIR_ELL_RD_LOLIM: f32 = 4.1033357e-26;\nconst PETIR_ELL_RD_UPLIM: f32 = 4.0234673e23;\nconst PETIR_ELL_RJ_LOLIM: f32 = 3.8880352e-13;\nconst PETIR_ELL_RJ_UPLIM: f32 = 1.2248354e12;\n// sqrt(f32::EPSILON), where Kcomp and Ecomp switch to the A&S series.\nconst PETIR_ELL_SQRT_EPS: f32 = 3.4526698e-4;\n\nfn petir_ell_nan() -> f32 { return bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u); }\n\nfn petir_ell_max3(x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32 { return max(max(x, y), z); }\nfn petir_ell_max4(x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, w: f32) -> f32 { return max(max(max(x, y), z), w); }\n\n// Carlson\'s R_C(x,y) = R_F(x,y,y).\nfn petir_ellint_rc(x: f32, y: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= 0.0) || !(y >= 0.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    if (x + y < PETIR_ELL_RF_LOLIM || max(x, y) >= PETIR_ELL_RF_UPLIM) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let c1 = 1.0 / 7.0;\n    let c2 = 9.0 / 22.0;\n    var xn = x;\n    var yn = y;\n    var mu = 0.0;\n    var sn = 0.0;\n    for (var n: u32 = 0u; n < PETIR_ELL_NMAX; n = n + 1u) {\n        mu = (xn + yn + yn) / 3.0;\n        sn = (yn + mu) / mu - 2.0;\n        if (abs(sn) < PETIR_ELL_ERRTOL) { break; }\n        let lamda = 2.0 * sqrt(xn) * sqrt(yn) + yn;\n        xn = (xn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        yn = (yn + lamda) * 0.25;\n    }\n    let s = sn * sn * (0.3 + sn * (c1 + sn * (0.375 + sn * c2)));\n    return (1.0 + s) / sqrt(mu);\n}\n\n// Carlson\'s R_D(x,y,z).\nfn petir_ellint_rd(x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= 0.0) || !(y >= 0.0) || !(z >= 0.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    if (min(x + y, z) < PETIR_ELL_RD_LOLIM) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    if (petir_ell_max3(x, y, z) >= PETIR_ELL_RD_UPLIM) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let c1 = 3.0 / 14.0;\n    let c2 = 1.0 / 6.0;\n    let c3 = 9.0 / 22.0;\n    let c4 = 3.0 / 26.0;\n    var xn = x;\n    var yn = y;\n    var zn = z;\n    var sigma = 0.0;\n    var power4 = 1.0;\n    var mu = 0.0;\n    var xndev = 0.0;\n    var yndev = 0.0;\n    var zndev = 0.0;\n    for (var n: u32 = 0u; n < PETIR_ELL_NMAX; n = n + 1u) {\n        mu = (xn + yn + 3.0 * zn) * 0.2;\n        xndev = (mu - xn) / mu;\n        yndev = (mu - yn) / mu;\n        zndev = (mu - zn) / mu;\n        if (petir_ell_max3(abs(xndev), abs(yndev), abs(zndev)) < PETIR_ELL_ERRTOL) { break; }\n        let xr = sqrt(xn);\n        let yr = sqrt(yn);\n        let zr = sqrt(zn);\n        let lamda = xr * (yr + zr) + yr * zr;\n        sigma = sigma + power4 / (zr * (zn + lamda));\n        power4 = power4 * 0.25;\n        xn = (xn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        yn = (yn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        zn = (zn + lamda) * 0.25;\n    }\n    let ea = xndev * yndev;\n    let eb = zndev * zndev;\n    let ec = ea - eb;\n    let ed = ea - 6.0 * eb;\n    let ef = ed + ec + ec;\n    let s1 = ed * (-c1 + 0.25 * c3 * ed - 1.5 * c4 * zndev * ef);\n    let s2 = zndev * (c2 * ef + zndev * (-c3 * ec + zndev * c4 * ea));\n    return 3.0 * sigma + power4 * (1.0 + s1 + s2) / (mu * sqrt(mu));\n}\n\n// Carlson\'s R_F(x,y,z).\nfn petir_ellint_rf(x: f32, y: f32, z: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= 0.0) || !(y >= 0.0) || !(z >= 0.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    if (x + y < PETIR_ELL_RF_LOLIM || x + z < PETIR_ELL_RF_LOLIM || y + z < PETIR_ELL_RF_LOLIM) {\n        return petir_ell_nan();\n    }\n    if (petir_ell_max3(x, y, z) >= PETIR_ELL_RF_UPLIM) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let c1 = 1.0 / 24.0;\n    let c2 = 3.0 / 44.0;\n    let c3 = 1.0 / 14.0;\n    var xn = x;\n    var yn = y;\n    var zn = z;\n    var mu = 0.0;\n    var xndev = 0.0;\n    var yndev = 0.0;\n    var zndev = 0.0;\n    for (var n: u32 = 0u; n < PETIR_ELL_NMAX; n = n + 1u) {\n        mu = (xn + yn + zn) / 3.0;\n        xndev = 2.0 - (mu + xn) / mu;\n        yndev = 2.0 - (mu + yn) / mu;\n        zndev = 2.0 - (mu + zn) / mu;\n        if (petir_ell_max3(abs(xndev), abs(yndev), abs(zndev)) < PETIR_ELL_ERRTOL) { break; }\n        let xr = sqrt(xn);\n        let yr = sqrt(yn);\n        let zr = sqrt(zn);\n        let lamda = xr * (yr + zr) + yr * zr;\n        xn = (xn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        yn = (yn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        zn = (zn + lamda) * 0.25;\n    }\n    let e2 = xndev * yndev - zndev * zndev;\n    let e3 = xndev * yndev * zndev;\n    let s = 1.0 + (c1 * e2 - 0.1 - c2 * e3) * e2 + c3 * e3;\n    return s / sqrt(mu);\n}\n\n// Carlson\'s R_J(x,y,z,p). Calls R_C once per duplication step -- a nested\n// call, not recursion, which WGSL permits.\nfn petir_ellint_rj(x: f32, y: f32, z: f32, p: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(x >= 0.0) || !(y >= 0.0) || !(z >= 0.0) || !(p >= 0.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    if (x + y < PETIR_ELL_RJ_LOLIM || x + z < PETIR_ELL_RJ_LOLIM\n        || y + z < PETIR_ELL_RJ_LOLIM || p < PETIR_ELL_RJ_LOLIM) {\n        return petir_ell_nan();\n    }\n    if (petir_ell_max4(x, y, z, p) >= PETIR_ELL_RJ_UPLIM) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let c1 = 3.0 / 14.0;\n    let c2 = 1.0 / 3.0;\n    let c3 = 3.0 / 22.0;\n    let c4 = 3.0 / 26.0;\n    var xn = x;\n    var yn = y;\n    var zn = z;\n    var pn = p;\n    var sigma = 0.0;\n    var power4 = 1.0;\n    var mu = 0.0;\n    var xndev = 0.0;\n    var yndev = 0.0;\n    var zndev = 0.0;\n    var pndev = 0.0;\n    for (var n: u32 = 0u; n < PETIR_ELL_NMAX; n = n + 1u) {\n        mu = (xn + yn + zn + pn + pn) * 0.2;\n        xndev = (mu - xn) / mu;\n        yndev = (mu - yn) / mu;\n        zndev = (mu - zn) / mu;\n        pndev = (mu - pn) / mu;\n        if (petir_ell_max4(abs(xndev), abs(yndev), abs(zndev), abs(pndev)) < PETIR_ELL_ERRTOL) {\n            break;\n        }\n        let xr = sqrt(xn);\n        let yr = sqrt(yn);\n        let zr = sqrt(zn);\n        let lamda = xr * (yr + zr) + yr * zr;\n        var alfa = pn * (xr + yr + zr) + xr * yr * zr;\n        alfa = alfa * alfa;\n        let beta = pn * (pn + lamda) * (pn + lamda);\n        let rcv = petir_ellint_rc(alfa, beta);\n        if (rcv != rcv) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n        sigma = sigma + power4 * rcv;\n        power4 = power4 * 0.25;\n        xn = (xn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        yn = (yn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        zn = (zn + lamda) * 0.25;\n        pn = (pn + lamda) * 0.25;\n    }\n    let ea = xndev * (yndev + zndev) + yndev * zndev;\n    let eb = xndev * yndev * zndev;\n    let ec = pndev * pndev;\n    let e2 = ea - 3.0 * ec;\n    let e3 = eb + 2.0 * pndev * (ea - ec);\n    let s1 = 1.0 + e2 * (-c1 + 0.75 * c3 * e2 - 1.5 * c4 * e3);\n    let s2 = eb * (0.5 * c2 + pndev * (-c3 - c3 + pndev * c4));\n    let s3 = pndev * ea * (c2 - pndev * c3) - c2 * pndev * ec;\n    return 3.0 * sigma + power4 * (s1 + s2 + s3) / (mu * sqrt(mu));\n}\n\n// The complete integrals.\nfn petir_ellint_kcomp(k: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(k * k < 1.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    if (k * k >= 1.0 - PETIR_ELL_SQRT_EPS) {\n        // A&S 17.3.34 -- K diverges logarithmically at k = 1 and no Carlson\n        // form can represent that.\n        let y = 1.0 - k * k;\n        let ta = 1.38629436112 + y * (0.09666344259 + y * 0.03590092383);\n        let tb = -log(y) * (0.5 + y * (0.12498593597 + y * 0.06880248576));\n        return ta + tb;\n    }\n    return petir_ellint_rf(0.0, 1.0 - k * k, 1.0);\n}\n\nfn petir_ellint_ecomp(k: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(k * k < 1.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    if (k * k >= 1.0 - PETIR_ELL_SQRT_EPS) {\n        // A&S 17.3.36.\n        let y = 1.0 - k * k;\n        let ta = 1.0 + y * (0.44325141463 + y * (0.06260601220 + 0.04757383546 * y));\n        let tb = -y * log(y) * (0.24998368310 + y * (0.09200180037 + 0.04069697526 * y));\n        return ta + tb;\n    }\n    let y = 1.0 - k * k;\n    return petir_ellint_rf(0.0, y, 1.0) - k * k / 3.0 * petir_ellint_rd(0.0, y, 1.0);\n}\n\nfn petir_ellint_dcomp(k: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(k * k < 1.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    return (1.0 / 3.0) * petir_ellint_rd(0.0, 1.0 - k * k, 1.0);\n}\n\nfn petir_ellint_pcomp(k: f32, n: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (!(k * k < 1.0)) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let y = 1.0 - k * k;\n    return petir_ellint_rf(0.0, y, 1.0) - (n / 3.0) * petir_ellint_rj(0.0, y, 1.0, 1.0 + n);\n}\n\n// The incomplete integrals. phi is reduced modulo pi with the periodicity\n// added back -- upstream\'s own reduction, which its comment calls approximate.\nfn petir_ellint_f(phi_in: f32, k: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (phi_in != phi_in || k != k) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let nc = floor(phi_in / 3.1415927 + 0.5);\n    let phi = phi_in - nc * 3.1415927;\n    let sp = sin(phi);\n    let s2 = sp * sp;\n    let v = sp * petir_ellint_rf(1.0 - s2, 1.0 - k * k * s2, 1.0);\n    if (nc == 0.0) { return v; }\n    return v + 2.0 * nc * petir_ellint_kcomp(k);\n}\n\nfn petir_ellint_e(phi_in: f32, k: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (phi_in != phi_in || k != k) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let nc = floor(phi_in / 3.1415927 + 0.5);\n    let phi = phi_in - nc * 3.1415927;\n    let sp = sin(phi);\n    let s2 = sp * sp;\n    let x = 1.0 - s2;\n    let y = 1.0 - k * k * s2;\n    if (x < 1.1920929e-7) {\n        let re = petir_ellint_ecomp(k);\n        return 2.0 * nc * re + sign(sp) * re;\n    }\n    let s3 = s2 * sp;\n    let v = sp * petir_ellint_rf(x, y, 1.0) - k * k / 3.0 * s3 * petir_ellint_rd(x, y, 1.0);\n    if (nc == 0.0) { return v; }\n    return v + 2.0 * nc * petir_ellint_ecomp(k);\n}\n\nfn petir_ellint_p(phi_in: f32, k: f32, n: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (phi_in != phi_in || k != k || n != n) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let nc = floor(phi_in / 3.1415927 + 0.5);\n    let phi = phi_in - nc * 3.1415927;\n    let sp = sin(phi);\n    let s2 = sp * sp;\n    let s3 = s2 * sp;\n    let x = 1.0 - s2;\n    let y = 1.0 - k * k * s2;\n    let v = sp * petir_ellint_rf(x, y, 1.0)\n          - n / 3.0 * s3 * petir_ellint_rj(x, y, 1.0, 1.0 + n * s2);\n    if (nc == 0.0) { return v; }\n    return v + 2.0 * nc * petir_ellint_pcomp(k, n);\n}\n\nfn petir_ellint_d(phi_in: f32, k: f32) -> f32 {\n    if (phi_in != phi_in || k != k) { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    let nc = floor(phi_in / 3.1415927 + 0.5);\n    let phi = phi_in - nc * 3.1415927;\n    let sp = sin(phi);\n    let s2 = sp * sp;\n    let s3 = s2 * sp;\n    let v = s3 / 3.0 * petir_ellint_rd(1.0 - s2, 1.0 - k * k * s2, 1.0);\n    if (nc == 0.0) { return v; }\n    return v + 2.0 * nc * petir_ellint_dcomp(k);\n}\n\n// One dispatcher over the four complete integrals, in the order K, E, D, Pi.\n// `n` is read only by Pi. Any other `which` gives NaN.\nfn petir_ellint_comp(which: u32, k: f32, n: f32) -> f32 {\n    switch (which) {\n        case 0u: { return petir_ellint_kcomp(k); }\n        case 1u: { return petir_ellint_ecomp(k); }\n        case 2u: { return petir_ellint_dcomp(k); }\n        case 3u: { return petir_ellint_pcomp(k, n); }\n        default: { return petir_ell_nan(); }\n    }\n}\n";
```

#### Constant `EXPINT`

The exponential integrals `E_1` and `Ei` and the hyperbolic sine and
cosine integrals `Shi` and `Chi`, ported from `specfunc/expint.c` and
`specfunc/shint.c` by way of [`crate::expint`] and
[`crate::specfunc::shint`].

Provides `petir_expint_e1`, `petir_expint_e1_scaled`, `petir_expint_ei`,
`petir_expint_ei_scaled`, `petir_shi`, `petir_chi` and the selector
`petir_expint_family(which, x)`, plus the seven Chebyshev series.

**Four functions from one branch tree** — `Ei` is `-E_1(-x)` and `Shi`,
`Chi` are its sum and difference with `E_1`. **Prefer the scaled entry
points on a GPU**: `E_1` underflows to zero past `x ~ 83`. See
[`mirror_expint`].

